format: Sentence-based chunks preserving line structure with Greek-English parallel text
greek_source: Thomas Taylor, The Mystical Hymns of Orpheus (London, 1787)
translation_note: English translations generated by GPT-5 reasoning system from original Greek texts

text.english: Learn, Musaeus, the very august rite of burnt-offering, a prayer which indeed for you is the foremost of all.
text.greek: Μάνθανε δὴ, Μουσαῖε, θυηπολίην περισέμνην, εὐχήν, ἣ δή τοι προφερεστέρη ἐστὶν ἁπασέων.

line_details.greek: Μάνθανε δὴ, Μουσαῖε, θυηπολίην περισέμνην,
line_details.english: Learn, Musaeus, the very august rite of burnt-offering,
line_details.note: θυηπολίη denotes the conducting of sacrifice, often of burnt‑offerings; Musaeus is the traditional pupil of Orpheus.

line_details.greek: εὐχήν, ἣ δή τοι προφερεστέρη ἐστὶν ἁπασέων.
line_details.english: a prayer which indeed for you is the foremost of all.
line_details.note: προφερεστέρη = “most preeminent, foremost.”

text.english: Zeus the king, and Gaia, and the holy heavenly flames of Hēlios, and the sacred radiance of Mēnē, and all the Stars; and you too, Poseidaon, earth-supporting, dark-maned, and holy Phersephonē, and Dēmētēr rich in fruit, and Artemis the arrow-showering, maiden, and gentle Phoibos, who dwell in the holy plain of Delphoi; and you who have the greatest honors among the Blessed, Dionysos, lord of the dance; and Ares of stormy heart, and the holy might of Hēphaistos, and the foam-born goddess, possessor of high-renowned gifts; and you, king of those below, surpassing great daimon; and Hēbē, Eileithyia, and the goodly might of Hēraklēs; and the great boon of Dikaiosynē and Eusebeia I invoke, and the famed Nymphs, and great Pan, and Hērā, the flourishing bedfellow of aegis-bearing Zeus; and lovely Mnēmosynē, and I call upon the holy nine Mousai, and the Kharites, and the Hōrai, and Eniautos, and Lētō of the fair tresses, divine, and august Diōnē, and the armed Kourētēs, and the Korybantes, and the Kabeiroi, and together the great Sōtēres, the imperishable children of Zeus; and the Idaian gods, and the messenger of the Ouranians, Hermēs the herald, and Themis, overseer of sacred rites among men, and Night the eldest I call, and light-bringing Day, and Pistis, and Dikē, and the blameless Law‑giving Lady; and Rheia, and Kronos, and Tēthys of the dark veil, and great Ōkeanos, together with the daughters of Ōkeanos, and the far‑superior strength of Atlas and Aiōn, and Chronos ever‑flowing, and the splendid water of Styx, and the Meilichioi gods, and, over these, Good Pronoia, and the kindly Daimōn and the baneful Daimōn of mortals, the heavenly and sea‑dwelling and water‑haunting daimones, and the chthonian and under‑chthonian, and those who roam the air, and Semelē, and all the fellow‑banqueters of Bakchos, and Inō Leukothēa, and Palaimōn, giver of bliss.
text.greek: Ζεῦ βασιλεῦ, καὶ Γαῖα, καὶ οὐράνιαι φλόγες ἁγναὶ Ἠελίου, Μήνης θ’ ἱερὸν σέλας, Ἄστρα τε πάντα· καὶ σύ, Ποσείδαον γαιήοχε κυανοχαῖτα, Φερσεφόνη θ' ἁγνή, Δημήτηρ τ' ἀγλαόκαρπε, Ἄρτεμί τ' ἰοχέαιρα, κόρη, καὶ ἤιε Φοῖβε, ὃς Δελφῶν ναίεις ἱερὸν πέδον· ὅς τε μεγίστας τιμὰς ἐν μακάρεσσιν ἔχεις, Διόνυσε χορευτά· Ἆρές τ' ὀμβριμόθυμε, καὶ Ἡφαίστου μένος ἁγνὸν, ἀφρογενής τε θεά, μεγαλώνυμα δῶρα λαχοῦσα· καὶ σύ, καταχθονίων βασιλεῦ, μέγ’ ὑπείροχε δαῖμον · Ἥβη τ’, Εἰλείθυια, καὶ Ἡρακλέος μένος ἠΰ· καὶ τὸ Δικαιοσύνης τε καὶ Εὐσεβίης μέγ' ὄνειαρ κικλήσκω, Νύμφας τε κλυτὰς, καὶ Πᾶνα μέγιστον, Ἥρην τ’, αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς θαλερὴν παράκοιτιν· Μνημοσύνην τ' ἐρατὴν, Μούσας τ' ἐπικέκλομαι ἁγνὰς ἐννέα καὶ Χάριτάς τε, καὶ Ὥρας, ἠδ' Ἐνιαυτὸν, Λητώ τ’ εὐπλόκαμον θείην σεμνήν τε Διώνην, Κουρ ῆτάς τ' ἐνόπλους Κορύβαντάς τ’, ἠδὲ Καβείρους, καὶ μεγάλους Σωτῆρας ὁμοῦ, Δι ὸς ἄφθιτα τέκνα· Ἰδαίους τε θεοὺς, ἠδ’ ἄ γγελον Οὐρανιώνων, Ἑρμείαν κήρυκα, Θέμιν θ’, ἱεροσκόπον ἀνδρ ῶν, Νύκτα τε πρεσβίστην καλέω, καὶ φωσφόρον Ἦμαρ, Πίστιν τ’, ἠδὲ Δίκην, καὶ ἀμύμονα Θεσμοδότειραν· Ῥείαν τ’, ἠδὲ Κρόνον, καὶ Τηθ ὺν κυανόπεπλον, Ὠκεανόν τε μέγαν, σύν τ ’ Ὠκεανοῖο θύγατρας Ἄτλαντός τε καὶ Αἰῶνος μέγ’ ὑπείροχον ἰσχύν· καὶ Χρόνον ἀέναον, καὶ τὸ Στυγὸς ἀγλαὸν ὕδωρ, Μειλιχίους τε θεούς· ἀγαθήν τ’ ἐπὶ τοῖσι Πρόνοιαν· Δαίμονά τ’ ἠγάθεον, καὶ Δαίμονα πήμονα θνητῶν· Δαίμονας οὐρανίους τε καὶ εἰναλίους καὶ ἐνύδρους, καὶ χθονίους καὶ ὑποχθονίους, ἠδ’ ἠεριφοίτους·, καὶ Σεμέλην, Βάκχου τε συνευαστῆρας ἅπαντας, Ἰνὼ Λευκοθέην τε, Παλαίμονά τ’ ὀλβιοδώτην.

line_details.greek: Ζεῦ βασιλεῦ, καὶ Γαῖα, καὶ οὐράνιαι φλόγες ἁγναὶ
line_details.english: Zeus the king, and Gaia, and the holy heavenly flames
line_details.note: “ouranian” = heavenly; the “flames of Hēlios” are his rays.

line_details.greek: Ἠελίου, Μήνης θ’ ἱερὸν σέλας, Ἄστρα τε πάντα·
line_details.english: of Hēlios, and the sacred radiance of Mēnē, and all the Stars;
line_details.note: Mēnē is the Moon personified; “sacred radiance” (ἱερὸν σέλας) suits lunar light.

line_details.greek: καὶ σύ, Ποσείδαον γαιήοχε κυανοχαῖτα,
line_details.english: and you too, Poseidaon, earth-supporting, dark-maned,
line_details.note: Poseidaon is an epic form of Poseidon; gaiēochos = “earth‑holding/supporting,” kyanochaitēs = “dark‑maned.”

line_details.greek: Φερσεφόνη θ' ἁγνή, Δημήτηρ τ' ἀγλαόκαρπε,
line_details.english: and holy Phersephonē, and Dēmētēr rich in fruit,
line_details.note: Phersephonē is an epic form of Persephonē; Dēmētēr’s epithet ἀγλαόκαρπος = “rich in fruit.”

line_details.greek: Ἄρτεμί τ' ἰοχέαιρα, κόρη, καὶ ἤιε Φοῖβε,
line_details.english: and Artemis the arrow-showering, maiden, and gentle Phoibos,
line_details.note: ἰοχέαιρα = “arrow‑pouring”; ἤιε = “gentle/kindly”; Phoibos here is Apollō.

line_details.greek: ὃς Δελφῶν ναίεις ἱερὸν πέδον· ὅς τε μεγίστας
line_details.english: who dwell in the holy plain of Delphoi; and you who have the greatest
line_details.note: Delphoi’s “holy plain” (ἱερὸν πέδον) marks Apollō’s precinct.

line_details.greek: τιμὰς ἐν μακάρεσσιν ἔχεις, Διόνυσε χορευτά·
line_details.english: honors among the Blessed, Dionysos, lord of the dance;
line_details.note: χορευτάς of Dionysos = “leader/lord of the dance,” suited to choral revelry.

line_details.greek: Ἆρές τ' ὀμβριμόθυμε, καὶ Ἡφαίστου μένος ἁγνὸν,
line_details.english: and Ares of stormy heart, and the holy might of Hēphaistos,
line_details.note: ὀμβριμόθυμος = “storm‑hearted, impetuous”; “holy might” (Ἡφαίστου μένος ἁγνόν) evokes sacred fire.

line_details.greek: ἀφρογενής τε θεά, μεγαλώνυμα δῶρα λαχοῦσα·
line_details.english: and the foam-born goddess, possessor of high-renowned gifts;
line_details.note: “foam‑born goddess” transparently indicates Aphroditē; μεγαλώνυμα δῶρα = “gifts of great renown.”

line_details.greek: καὶ σύ, καταχθονίων βασιλεῦ, μέγ’ ὑπείροχε δαῖμον ·
line_details.english: and you, king of those below, surpassing great daimon;
line_details.note: “king of those below” = lord of the underworld (Aidēs/Ploutōn); δαῖμον here = a divine power, not “demon.”

line_details.greek: Ἥβη τ’, Εἰλείθυια, καὶ Ἡρακλέος μένος ἠΰ·
line_details.english: and Hēbē, Eileithyia, and the goodly might of Hēraklēs;
line_details.note: Eileithyia is goddess of childbirth; “goodly might” (ἠϋ‑) of Hēraklēs is honorific.

line_details.greek: καὶ τὸ Δικαιοσύνης τε καὶ Εὐσεβίης μέγ' ὄνειαρ
line_details.english: and the great boon of Dikaiosynē and Eusebeia
line_details.note: Dikaiosynē (Justice) and Eusebeia (Piety) are personified abstractions.

line_details.greek: κικλήσκω, Νύμφας τε κλυτὰς, καὶ Πᾶνα μέγιστον,
line_details.english: I invoke, and the famed Nymphs, and great Pan,

line_details.greek: Ἥρην τ’, αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς θαλερὴν παράκοιτιν·
line_details.english: and Hērā, the flourishing bedfellow of aegis-bearing Zeus;
line_details.note: aigiokhoios is Zeus’ set epithet “aegis‑bearing”; παράκοιτις = “bedfellow, consort.”

line_details.greek: Μνημοσύνην τ' ἐρατὴν, Μούσας τ' ἐπικέκλομαι ἁγνὰς
line_details.english: and lovely Mnēmosynē, and I call upon the holy

line_details.greek: ἐννέα καὶ Χάριτάς τε, καὶ Ὥρας, ἠδ' Ἐνιαυτὸν,
line_details.english: nine Mousai, and the Kharites, and the Hōrai, and Eniautos,
line_details.note: Hōrai (Seasons) and Eniautos (the Year) are temporal personifications.

line_details.greek: Λητώ τ’ εὐπλόκαμον θείην σεμνήν τε Διώνην,
line_details.english: and Lētō of the fair tresses, divine, and august Diōnē,
line_details.note: Diōnē is a venerable goddess, sometimes a mother of Aphroditē.

line_details.greek: Κουρ ῆτάς τ' ἐνόπλους Κορύβαντάς τ’, ἠδὲ Καβείρους,
line_details.english: and the armed Kourētēs, and the Korybantes, and the Kabeiroi,
line_details.note: Kourētēs, Korybantes, Kabeiroi: armed/dancing attendants of the Mother and mystery‑deities.

line_details.greek: καὶ μεγάλους Σωτῆρας ὁμοῦ, Δι ὸς ἄφθιτα τέκνα·
line_details.english: and together the great Sōtēres, the imperishable children of Zeus;
line_details.note: Sōtēres likely the Dioskouroi (“Saviors”), called imperishable children of Zeus.

line_details.greek: Ἰδαίους τε θεοὺς, ἠδ’ ἄ γγελον Οὐρανιώνων,
line_details.english: and the Idaian gods, and the messenger of the Ouranians,
line_details.note: The “Idaian gods” are Cretan (linked to Mount Ida); “messenger of the Ouranians” anticipates Hermēs.

line_details.greek: Ἑρμείαν κήρυκα, Θέμιν θ’, ἱεροσκόπον ἀνδρ ῶν,
line_details.english: Hermēs the herald, and Themis, overseer of sacred rites among men,
line_details.note: ἱεροσκόπος of Themis = “overseer/interpreter of sacred matters” among humans.

line_details.greek: Νύκτα τε πρεσβίστην καλέω, καὶ φωσφόρον Ἦμαρ,
line_details.english: and Night the eldest I call, and light-bringing Day,
line_details.note: Nyx is called “eldest”; Day (Ἦμαρ) is “light‑bringing.”

line_details.greek: Πίστιν τ’, ἠδὲ Δίκην, καὶ ἀμύμονα Θεσμοδότειραν·
line_details.english: and Pistis, and Dikē, and the blameless Law‑giving Lady;
line_details.note: Pistis = Trust/Good Faith; “blameless Law‑giving Lady” (Θεσμοδότειρα) may allude to Themis or Demeter as lawgiver.

line_details.greek: Ῥείαν τ’, ἠδὲ Κρόνον, καὶ Τηθ ὺν κυανόπεπλον,
line_details.english: and Rheia, and Kronos, and Tēthys of the dark veil,
line_details.note: κυανόπεπλος = “dark‑veiled,” a marine epithet of Tēthys; Rheia = Rhea.

line_details.greek: Ὠκεανόν τε μέγαν, σύν τ
line_details.english: and great Ōkeanos, together
line_details.note: Lines 27–28 form one syntactic unit: Ōkeanos with his daughters (the Oceanids).

line_details.greek: ’ Ὠκεανοῖο θύγατρας
line_details.english: with the daughters of Ōkeanos,

line_details.greek: Ἄτλαντός τε καὶ Αἰῶνος μέγ’ ὑπείροχον ἰσχύν·
line_details.english: and the far‑superior strength of Atlas and Aiōn,
line_details.note: Aiōn (Eternity, cyclical time) differs from Chronos (line 30), often linear/temporal succession.

line_details.greek: καὶ Χρόνον ἀέναον, καὶ τὸ Στυγὸς ἀγλαὸν ὕδωρ,
line_details.english: and Chronos ever‑flowing, and the splendid water of Styx,
line_details.note: Chronos “ever‑flowing” contrasts with Aiōn; Styx’s waters are the most solemn oath for gods.

line_details.greek: Μειλιχίους τε θεούς· ἀγαθήν τ’ ἐπὶ τοῖσι Πρόνοιαν·
line_details.english: and the Meilichioi gods, and, over these, Good Pronoia,
line_details.note: Meilichioi (“Gracious/Placatory”) are often euphemistic cthonic powers; Pronoia = Providence.

line_details.greek: Δαίμονά τ’ ἠγάθεον, καὶ Δαίμονα πήμονα θνητῶν·
line_details.english: and the kindly Daimōn and the baneful Daimōn of mortals,
line_details.note: Daimōn = neutral “divine agency”; here benevolent vs. baneful toward mortals.

line_details.greek: Δαίμονας οὐρανίους τε καὶ εἰναλίους καὶ ἐνύδρους,
line_details.english: the heavenly and sea‑dwelling and water‑haunting daimones,

line_details.greek: καὶ χθονίους καὶ ὑποχθονίους, ἠδ’ ἠεριφοίτους·,
line_details.english: and the chthonian and under‑chthonian, and those who roam the air,
line_details.note: ἠεριφοίτους = “air‑roaming,” of aerial spirits.

line_details.greek: καὶ Σεμέλην, Βάκχου τε συνευαστῆρας ἅπαντας,
line_details.english: and Semelē, and all the fellow‑banqueters of Bakchos,
line_details.note: “fellow‑banqueters of Bakchos” = Bacchic companions/initiates (thiasoi).

line_details.greek: Ἰνὼ Λευκοθέην τε, Παλαίμονά τ’ ὀλβιοδώτην.
line_details.english: and Inō Leukothēa, and Palaimōn, giver of bliss.
line_details.note: Inō deified as Leukothea; Palaimōn (Melikertes) a sea‑helper god.

text.english: [and Nikē, the sweet‑speaking one, and Queen Adrēsteia, and great king Asklēpios, gentle in giving aid.] and Pallas, the battle‑awakening maiden, and all the Winds, and the Thunders, and I proclaim the fourfold parts of the Cosmos, and I call the Mother of the immortals, and Attis and Mēn, and the Ouranian goddess, together with immortal, holy Adōnis, and both Archē and Peras (for this is greatest for all), to come gracious, possessing a gladdened heart, to this holy rite of burnt‑offering, and to the august libation.
text.greek: [Νίκην θ’ ἡ δυέπειαν, ἰδ’ Ἀδρήστειαν ἄνασσαν· καὶ βασιλῆα μέγαν Ἀσκληπιὸν ἠπιοδώτην.] Παλλάδα τ’ ἐγρεμάχην κούρην, Ἀνέμους τε πρόπαντας, καὶ Βροντὰς, Κόσμου τε μέρη τετρακίονος αὐδῶ· Μητέρα τ’ ἀθανάτων, Ἄττιν καὶ Μῆνα κικλήσκω, Οὐρανίην τε θεάν, σύν δ’ ἄμβροτον ἁγνὸν Ἄδωνιν, Ἀρχήν τ’ ἠδὲ Πέρας · (τὸ γὰρ ἔπλετο πᾶσι μέγιστον) ἐλθεῖν εὐμενέας, κεχαρημένον ἦτορ ἔχοντας, τήνδε θυηπολίην ἱερὴν, σπονδήν τ' ἐπὶ σεμνήν.

line_details.greek: [Νίκην θ’ ἡ δυέπειαν, ἰδ’ Ἀδρήστειαν ἄνασσαν·
line_details.english: [and Nikē, the sweet‑speaking one, and Queen Adrēsteia,
line_details.note: Bracketed lines are textually uncertain; ἡ δυέπειαν is likely corrupt, often emended to ἡδυεπῆ (“sweet‑speaking”); some witnesses omit these lines.

line_details.greek: καὶ βασιλῆα μέγαν Ἀσκληπιὸν ἠπιοδώτην.]
line_details.english: and great king Asklēpios, gentle in giving aid.]
line_details.note: Asklēpios’ epithet ἠπιοδώτης = “gentle in giving aid.”

line_details.greek: Παλλάδα τ’ ἐγρεμάχην κούρην, Ἀνέμους τε πρόπαντας,
line_details.english: and Pallas, the battle‑awakening maiden, and all the Winds,
line_details.note: ἐγρεμάχη = “battle‑awakening,” a martial epithet of Pallas (Athena).

line_details.greek: καὶ Βροντὰς, Κόσμου τε μέρη τετρακίονος αὐδῶ·
line_details.english: and the Thunders, and I proclaim the fourfold parts of the Cosmos,
line_details.note: “fourfold parts of the Cosmos” may denote the quarters of the world or elemental tetrad.

line_details.greek: Μητέρα τ’ ἀθανάτων, Ἄττιν καὶ Μῆνα κικλήσκω,
line_details.english: and I call the Mother of the immortals, and Attis and Mēn,
line_details.note: “Mother of the immortals” is the Mother of the Gods (Meter Theōn, Cybele/Rhea); Attis and Mēn are her Phrygian associates.

line_details.greek: Οὐρανίην τε θεάν, σύν δ’ ἄμβροτον ἁγνὸν Ἄδωνιν,
line_details.english: and the Ouranian goddess, together with immortal, holy Adōnis,
line_details.note: “Ouranian goddess” likely Aphroditē Ourania; Adōnis is the beloved youth of her cult.

line_details.greek: Ἀρχήν τ’ ἠδὲ Πέρας · (τὸ γὰρ ἔπλετο πᾶσι μέγιστον)
line_details.english: and both Archē and Peras (for this is greatest for all),
line_details.note: Archē and Peras (Beginning and End) are Orphic metaphysical principles, invoked as deities.

line_details.greek: ἐλθεῖν εὐμενέας, κεχαρημένον ἦτορ ἔχοντας,
line_details.english: to come gracious, possessing a gladdened heart,

line_details.greek: τήνδε θυηπολίην ἱερὴν, σπονδήν τ' ἐπὶ σεμνήν.
line_details.english: to this holy rite of burnt‑offering, and to the august libation.

text.english: I invoke Hekate Einodia, of the three-way crossroads, lovely, heavenly, chthonian, and seaborne, saffron-robed, of the tombs, reveling Bacchically among the souls of the dead, Perseia, fond of solitude, exulting in deer, nocturnal, of the whelps, the unconquerable queen, Bull-driving, key-bearing queen of the whole cosmos, guide, nymph, nurse of youths, mountain-roving, being implored, Maiden, be present at holy rites for the suppliants, ever gracious to the herdsman, with a gladdened heart.
text.greek: Εἰνοδίην Ἑκάτην κλῄιζω, τριοδῖτιν, ἐραννήν, οὐρανίην, χθονίαν τε, καὶ εἰναλίην κροκόπεπλον, τυμβιδίην, ψυχαῖς νεκύων μέτα βακχεύουσαν, Πέρσειαν, φιλέρημον, ἀγαλλομένην ἐλάφοισιν, νυκτερίην, σκυλακῖτιν, ἀμαιμάκετον βασίλειαν, ταυροπόλον, παντὸς κόσμου κληιδοῦχον ἄνασσαν, ἡγεμόνην, νύμφην, κουροτρόφον, οὐρεσιφοῖτιν, λισσομένοις κούρην τελεταῖς ὁσίαισι παρεῖναι βουκόλῳ εὐμενέουσαν ἀεὶ κεχαρηότι θυμῷ.

line_details.greek: Εἰνοδίην Ἑκάτην κλῄιζω, τριοδῖτιν, ἐραννήν,
line_details.english: I invoke Hekate Einodia, of the three-way crossroads, lovely,
line_details.note: Einodia (“of/along the roads”) and Trioditis (“of the three-way [crossroads]”) are traditional epithets of Hekate as a liminal road-goddess; I retain Einodia to preserve the cult title.

line_details.greek: οὐρανίην, χθονίαν τε, καὶ εἰναλίην κροκόπεπλον,
line_details.english: heavenly, chthonian, and seaborne, saffron-robed,
line_details.note: Einalia = “of the sea”; krokopeplos (“saffron-robed”) evokes the saffron-dyed garments associated with goddesses in ritual contexts.

line_details.greek: τυμβιδίην, ψυχαῖς νεκύων μέτα βακχεύουσαν,
line_details.english: of the tombs, reveling Bacchically among the souls of the dead,
line_details.note: Tymbidia = “of the tombs”; baccheuousan (“reveling in Bacchic frenzy”) aligns Hekate with Dionysiac rites in the underworld, reveling “among the souls of the dead” (psychais nekyōn).

line_details.greek: Πέρσειαν, φιλέρημον, ἀγαλλομένην ἐλάφοισιν,
line_details.english: Perseia, fond of solitude, exulting in deer,
line_details.note: Perseia is a patronymic (“daughter of Perses”) known from Hesiod; “exulting in deer” (agallomenēn elaphoisin) recalls Artemis’ venatic sphere, here applied to Hekate.

line_details.greek: νυκτερίην, σκυλακῖτιν, ἀμαιμάκετον βασίλειαν,
line_details.english: nocturnal, of the whelps, the unconquerable queen,
line_details.note: Skylakitin literally “associated with whelps/puppies,” marking her canine retinue; I render it idiomatically while noting the etymology. Amaimaketos = “unconquerable/irresistible.”

line_details.greek: ταυροπόλον, παντὸς κόσμου κληιδοῦχον ἄνασσαν,
line_details.english: Bull-driving, key-bearing queen of the whole cosmos,
line_details.note: Tauropolos/Tauropolon is debated (“bull-driving,” “bull-slayer,” or “bull-worshipped”); I choose “bull-driving.” Kleidouchos (“key-bearer”) is a cult title, here magnified as “of the whole cosmos.”

line_details.greek: ἡγεμόνην, νύμφην, κουροτρόφον, οὐρεσιφοῖτιν,
line_details.english: guide, nymph, nurse of youths, mountain-roving,
line_details.note: Nymphē can mean “nymph/maiden” rather than “bride” here; kourotrophos is a technical epithet for a deity who nurtures the young; ouresiphōitin = “mountain-roving.”

line_details.greek: λισσομένοις κούρην τελεταῖς ὁσίαισι παρεῖναι
line_details.english: being implored, Maiden, be present at holy rites for the suppliants,
line_details.note: Lissomenois is a dative of advantage (“for the suppliants”); teletai hosiai are “holy rites/initiations,” and pareinai (inf.) is the standard hymnic request “to be present/attend.”

line_details.greek: βουκόλῳ εὐμενέουσαν ἀεὶ κεχαρηότι θυμῷ.
line_details.english: ever gracious to the herdsman, with a gladdened heart.
line_details.note: Boukolos (“herdsman/cowherd”) likely voices the singer’s persona (Orphic/poetic shepherd); kecharēōti thymō(i) is a formulaic “with a gladdened heart,” here marking favorable divine disposition.

text.english: Hear me, O most-august goddess, much-named daimon, helper in birth-pangs, sweet in aspect to women in childbed; savior of women, sole child-loving one, gentle of mind, swift-delivering, a helper amid mortals’ pains, Prothyraia.
text.greek: Κλῦθί μοι, ὦ πολύσεμνε θεά, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον, ὠδίνων ἐπαρωγέ, λεχῶν ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι· θηλειῶν σώτειρα, μόνη φιλόπαις, ἀγανόφρον, ὠκυλόχεια, ἐπαρώγ’ ἀνίαις θνητῶν, Προθυραία.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθί μοι, ὦ πολύσεμνε θεά, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον,
line_details.english: Hear me, O most-august goddess, much-named daimon,
line_details.note: daimon here means a divine power or numen, not a malevolent “demon”; πολύσεμνος = “most-august,” πολυώνυμος = “much-named, of many epithets.”

line_details.greek: ὠδίνων ἐπαρωγέ, λεχῶν ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι·
line_details.english: helper in birth-pangs, sweet in aspect to women in childbed;
line_details.note: λεχώς (gen. λεχῶν) denotes a woman in childbed; ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι = “sweet to the sight,” i.e., pleasing in appearance/presence to those in labor.

line_details.greek: θηλειῶν σώτειρα, μόνη φιλόπαις, ἀγανόφρον,
line_details.english: savior of women, sole child-loving one, gentle of mind,
line_details.note: θῆλυ = “female, woman”; μόνη φιλόπαις = “sole child-loving,” highlighting exclusive concern for infants/children; ἀγανόφρων = “gentle-minded.”

line_details.greek: ὠκυλόχεια, ἐπαρώγ’ ἀνίαις θνητῶν, Προθυραία.
line_details.english: swift-delivering, a helper amid mortals’ pains, Prothyraia.
line_details.note: ὠκυλόχεια = “swift in delivery/bringing quick birth”; Προθυραία (“Before-the-door”) is a childbirth epithet linked to the threshold of the birthing-room.

text.english: key-bearing, propitious to meet, fond of nurture, gracious to all, you who hold the households of all, and you rejoice in banquets, girdle-loosener, unseen, yet in your works you appear to all, you share in the birth-pangs and you rejoice in easy deliveries, Eileithyia, loosening pains amid dreadful constraints.
text.greek: κλειδοῦχ’, εὐάντητε, φιλότροφε, πᾶσι προσηνής, ἣ κατέχεις οἴκους πάντων, θαλίαις τε γέγηθας, λυσίζων’, ἀφανής, ἔργοισι δὲ φαίνῃ ἅπασιν, συμπάσχεις ὠδῖσι καὶ εὐτοκί ῃσι γέγηθας, Εἰλείθυια, λύουσα πόνους δειναῖς ἐν ἀνάγκαις.

line_details.greek: κλειδοῦχ’, εὐάντητε, φιλότροφε, πᾶσι προσηνής,
line_details.english: key-bearing, propitious to meet, fond of nurture, gracious to all,
line_details.note: κλειδοῦχος = “key-bearing,” a marker of custodial/threshold authority; εὐάντητος = “of auspicious meeting, propitious to encounter”; φιλότροφος = “fond of nurture/rearing.”

line_details.greek: ἣ κατέχεις οἴκους πάντων, θαλίαις τε γέγηθας,
line_details.english: you who hold the households of all, and you rejoice in banquets,
line_details.note: θαλίαι can denote feasts generally and often wedding- or household-celebrations, fitting the domestic/ritual context.

line_details.greek: λυσίζων’, ἀφανής, ἔργοισι δὲ φαίνῃ ἅπασιν,
line_details.english: girdle-loosener, unseen, yet in your works you appear to all,
line_details.note: λυσιζών’ = “loosener of the girdle (zōnē),” a conventional epithet in contexts of marriage and childbirth; ἀφανής/φαίνῃ contrasts the goddess’s invisibility with her manifest effects.

line_details.greek: συμπάσχεις ὠδῖσι καὶ εὐτοκί ῃσι γέγηθας,
line_details.english: you share in the birth-pangs and you rejoice in easy deliveries,
line_details.note: συμπάσχειν = “to suffer with,” implying sympathetic presence; εὐτοκία = “easy/successful delivery.”

line_details.greek: Εἰλείθυια, λύουσα πόνους δειναῖς ἐν ἀνάγκαις.
line_details.english: Eileithyia, loosening pains amid dreadful constraints.
line_details.note: δειναὶ ἀνάγκαι = “dread constraints/necessities,” a formula for the extremity of labor; λύειν πόνους = “to loosen/relieve pains.”

text.english: for women in childbed call upon you alone, the soul’s repose.
text.greek: μούνην γάρ σ ὲ καλοῦσι λεχοί, ψυχ ῆς ἀνάπαυμα.

line_details.greek: μούνην γάρ σ ὲ καλοῦσι λεχοί, ψυχ ῆς ἀνάπαυμα.
line_details.english: for women in childbed call upon you alone, the soul’s repose.
line_details.note: ψυχῆς ἀνάπαυμα = “repose/relief of the soul,” i.e., mental solace for those in childbed.

text.english: for in you the sorrows of childbirth are made to be forgotten.
text.greek: ἐν γάρ σοὶ τοκετῶν λαθιπήμονές εἰσιν ἀνίαι.

line_details.greek: ἐν γάρ σοὶ τοκετῶν λαθιπήμονές εἰσιν ἀνίαι.
line_details.english: for in you the sorrows of childbirth are made to be forgotten.
line_details.note: λαθιπήμονες (“forgetful-of-suffering”) is a rare compound: the pains become such as to be forgotten—i.e., are made forgettable through the goddess’s aid.

text.english: Artemis Eileithyia, and revered Prothyraia, hear, blessed one; grant births, being present as a helper, and save, as you are by nature ever the savior before all.
text.greek: Ἄρτεμις Εἰλείθυια, καὶ εὐσέμνη Προθυραία. κλῦθι, μάκαιρα· δίδου δὲ γονάς, ἐπαρωγὸς ἐοῦσα καὶ σῶζε, ὥσπερ ἔφυς αἰεὶ σώτειρα προπάντων.

line_details.greek: Ἄρτεμις Εἰλείθυια, καὶ
line_details.english: Artemis Eileithyia, and
line_details.note: The hymn identifies Artemis with Eileithyia, reflecting overlapping roles in childbirth cult.

line_details.greek: εὐσέμνη Προθυραία.
line_details.english: revered Prothyraia,
line_details.note: εὐσέμνη = “revered, august”; Προθυραία reiterates the threshold epithet associated with childbirth rites.

line_details.greek: κλῦθι, μάκαιρα· δίδου δὲ γονάς, ἐπαρωγὸς ἐοῦσα
line_details.english: hear, blessed one; grant births, being present as a helper,
line_details.note: γόνας can mean “births” or “offspring”; in prayer context, “grant births” = grant successful delivery; ἐπαρωγός = “helper, aid.”

line_details.greek: καὶ σῶζε, ὥσπερ ἔφυς αἰεὶ σώτειρα προπάντων.
line_details.english: and save, as you are by nature ever the savior before all.
line_details.note: προπάντων can mean “before all others” (preeminent) or “on behalf of all”; “savior before all” preserves the elevated, preeminent sense.

text.english: I shall sing of Nyx, begetress of gods and of men.
text.greek: Νύκτα θεῶν γενέτειραν ἀείσομαι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρ ῶν.

line_details.greek: Νύκτα θεῶν γενέτειραν ἀείσομαι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρ ῶν.
line_details.english: I shall sing of Nyx, begetress of gods and of men.

text.english: Nyx, genesis of all things, whom we will also call Kypris.
text.greek: [Νὺξ γένεσις πάντων, ἣν καὶ Κύπριν καλέσωμεν]

line_details.greek: [Νὺξ γένεσις πάντων, ἣν καὶ Κύπριν καλέσωμεν]
line_details.english: Nyx, genesis of all things, whom we will also call Kypris.
line_details.note: Bracketed line: many editors mark it as interpolated. “Kypris” is Aphrodite; the identification of Nyx with the universal generative principle is Orphic in tone but textually suspect.

text.english: Hear, blessed goddess, dark-blue-gleaming, star-bright; rejoicing in quiet and in stillness rich in sleep; mirthful, delightful, lover of all-night vigils, mother of dreams; care-forgetting, possessing a good respite from toils; giver of sleep, beloved of all, chariot-driving, night-luminous; half-complete, chthonian, and again the same, heavenly; all-encircling, sporting in the chases of those who wander in mist; who send forth light beneath to the nether regions, and again you flee into Hades; for dread Anankê prevails over all.
text.greek: κλῦθι, μάκαιρα θεά, κυαναυγής, ἀστεροφεγγής· ἡσυχί ῃ χαίρουσα καὶ ἠ ρεμί ῃ πολυύπνῳ· εὐφροσύνη, τερπνή, φιλοπάννυχε, μῆτερ ὀνείρων· ληθομέριμν’, ἀγαθήν τε πόνων ἀνάπαυσιν ἔχουσα · ὑπνοδότειρα, φίλη πάντων, ἐλάσιππε, νυχαυγής· ἡμιτελής, χθονίη, ἠδ’ οὐρανίη πάλιν α ὐτή· ἐγκυκλίη, παίκτειρα διώγμασιν ἠεροφοίτοις· ἣ φάος ἐκπέμπεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα, καὶ πάλι φεύγεις εἰς Ἀΐδην. δειν ὴ γὰρ ἀνάγκη πάντα κρατύνει.

line_details.greek: κλῦθι, μάκαιρα θεά, κυαναυγής, ἀστεροφεγγής·
line_details.english: Hear, blessed goddess, dark-blue-gleaming, star-bright;

line_details.greek: ἡσυχί ῃ χαίρουσα καὶ ἠ ρεμί ῃ πολυύπνῳ·
line_details.english: rejoicing in quiet and in stillness rich in sleep;
line_details.note: “πολυύπνῳ” = “rich in sleep.” The line emphasizes Nyx’s quiet and soporific stillness.

line_details.greek: εὐφροσύνη, τερπνή, φιλοπάννυχε, μῆτερ ὀνείρων·
line_details.english: mirthful, delightful, lover of all-night vigils, mother of dreams;
line_details.note: “φιλοπάννυχε” literally “fond of all-night (vigils/festivals),” alluding to the ritual παννυχίς; hence “lover of all-night vigils.”

line_details.greek: ληθομέριμν’, ἀγαθήν τε πόνων ἀνάπαυσιν ἔχουσα ·
line_details.english: care-forgetting, possessing a good respite from toils;
line_details.note: “ληθομέριμν’” can mean “forgetting cares” or “causing forgetfulness of cares”; the translation reflects the latter nuance. “ἀνάπαυσις” = “respite/repose.”

line_details.greek: ὑπνοδότειρα, φίλη πάντων, ἐλάσιππε, νυχαυγής·
line_details.english: giver of sleep, beloved of all, chariot-driving, night-luminous;
line_details.note: “ἐλάσιππε” = “driver of horses,” i.e., of a night-chariot. “νυχαυγής” = “shining by night.”

line_details.greek: ἡμιτελής, χθονίη, ἠδ’ οὐρανίη πάλιν α ὐτή·
line_details.english: half-complete, chthonian, and again the same, heavenly;
line_details.note: “ἡμιτελής” (“half-complete”) is commonly taken of Night as half the cycle of time. “πάλιν αὐτή” is textually awkward; here understood as “and again the same, heavenly,” i.e., both chthonian and celestial.

line_details.greek: ἐγκυκλίη, παίκτειρα διώγμασιν ἠεροφοίτοις·
line_details.english: all-encircling, sporting in the chases of those who wander in mist;
line_details.note: “ἐγκυκλίη” = “all-encircling” (of the cosmic circuit). “παίκτειρα διώγμασιν ἠεροφοίτοις” is obscure: “sporting in the chases of those who wander in mist,” i.e., amid nocturnal, mist-roaming pursuits (perhaps of spirits or creatures).

line_details.greek: ἣ φάος ἐκπέμπεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα, καὶ πάλι φεύγεις
line_details.english: who send forth light beneath to the nether regions, and again you flee
line_details.note: “ὑπὸ νέρτερα” with ὑπό + acc is difficult: likely “beneath, to the nether regions.” Some take it “from beneath the lower world.” The sending of “light” may refer to moon/starlight seen from below or to a cosmological cycle.

line_details.greek: εἰς Ἀΐδην. δειν ὴ γὰρ ἀνάγκη πάντα κρατύνει.
line_details.english: into Hades; for dread Anankê prevails over all.
line_details.note: “Anankê” (Necessity) personified; “κρατύνει” = “prevails over/rules.”

text.english: But now, O blessed Nyx, much-wealthy, longed-for by all, gracious in meeting, hearing the suppliant voice of my words, come benevolent, and send away the night-gleaming fears.
text.greek: νῦν δὲ, μάκαιρ’ ὦ Ν ὺξ πολυόλβιε, πᾶσι ποθεινή, εὐάντητε, κλύουσα λόγων ἱκετηρίδα φωνὴν, ἔλθοις εὐμενέουσα, φόβους δ’ ἀπόπεμπε νυχαυγεῖς.

line_details.greek: νῦν δὲ, μάκαιρ’ ὦ Ν ὺξ πολυόλβιε, πᾶσι ποθεινή,
line_details.english: But now, O blessed Nyx, much-wealthy, longed-for by all,

line_details.greek: εὐάντητε, κλύουσα λόγων ἱκετηρίδα φωνὴν,
line_details.english: gracious in meeting, hearing the suppliant voice of my words,
line_details.note: “εὐάντητε” is a rare vocative/adjectival form, “gracious in meeting/approach.” “λόγων ἱκετηρίδα φωνήν” = “the suppliant voice of my words.”

line_details.greek: ἔλθοις εὐμενέουσα, φόβους δ’ ἀπόπεμπε νυχαυγεῖς.
line_details.english: come benevolent, and send away the night-gleaming fears.
line_details.note: “νυχαυγεῖς φόβους” = “night-gleaming fears,” i.e., terrors/phantoms that arise or seem to gleam in the night.

text.english: Ouranos, all-begetter, the ever-unwearied portion of the cosmos, ancient-born, the beginning of all things and the end of all, world-ruler, rolling like a sphere around the earth, house of the blessed gods, moving along in the vortices of the whirling rhombos, both heavenly and chthonian, guardian of all, enfolding them round about, holding within your breast the boundless Necessity of Nature, dark-blue in hue, indomitable, all-variegated, changeful of form, all-seeing, child of Kronos, blessed, most-exalted daimon, hear, and bring holy life to the newly revealed mystes.
text.greek: Οὐρανὲ παγγενέτωρ, κόσμου μέρος αἰὲν ἀτειρές, πρεσβυγένεθλ’, ἀρχ ὴ πάντων, πάντων τε τελευτή, κοσμοκράτωρ, σφαιρηδὸν ἑλισσόμενος περὶ γαῖαν, οἶκε θεῶν μακάρων, ῥόμβου δίνῃσιν ὁδεύων, οὐράνιος χθόνιός τε φύλαξ πάντων περιβληθείς· ἐν στέρνοισιν ἔχων φύσεως ἄπλητον ἀνάγκην, κυανόχρως, ἀδάμαστε, παναίολος, αἰολόμορφε, πανδερκές, Κρονότεκνε, μάκαρ, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον, κλῦθ’ ἐπάγων ζωὴν ὁσίην μύστῃ νεοφάντῃ.

line_details.greek: Οὐρανὲ παγγενέτωρ, κόσμου μέρος αἰὲν ἀτειρές,
line_details.english: Ouranos, all-begetter, the ever-unwearied portion of the cosmos,
line_details.note: κόσμου μέρος αἰὲν ἀτειρές: μέρος presents Ouranos as the upper “portion” of the ordered world; ἀτειρές = “unwearied, unworn.”

line_details.greek: πρεσβυγένεθλ’, ἀρχ ὴ πάντων, πάντων τε τελευτή,
line_details.english: ancient-born, the beginning of all things and the end of all,
line_details.note: πρεσβυγένεθλ’ is a contracted vocative, “ancient-born,” i.e., born before all. ἀρχὴ … τελευτή balances “beginning/end” as cosmological first principle and telos.

line_details.greek: κοσμοκράτωρ, σφαιρηδὸν ἑλισσόμενος περὶ γαῖαν,
line_details.english: world-ruler, rolling like a sphere around the earth,
line_details.note: σφαιρηδόν is an adverb, “in spherical fashion,” evoking the rotation of the celestial sphere about the earth.

line_details.greek: οἶκε θεῶν μακάρων, ῥόμβου δίνῃσιν ὁδεύων,
line_details.english: house of the blessed gods, moving along in the vortices of the whirling rhombos,
line_details.note: ῥόμβος is the whirring “rhombos” (bull‑roarer/spinning disc) and here symbolizes cosmic rotation; δίναι are its eddies/vortices.

line_details.greek: οὐράνιος χθόνιός τε φύλαξ πάντων περιβληθείς·
line_details.english: both heavenly and chthonian, guardian of all, enfolding them round about,
line_details.note: οὐράνιος χθόνιός τε pairs seemingly opposed realms; Ouranos is imagined as encompassing above and below. περιβληθείς literally “clothed about, enfolding.”

line_details.greek: ἐν στέρνοισιν ἔχων φύσεως ἄπλητον ἀνάγκην,
line_details.english: holding within your breast the boundless Necessity of Nature,
line_details.note: φύσεως ἄπλητον ἀνάγκην: ἀνάγκη (“necessity”) may hint at the Orphic cosmic Necessity; ἄπλητος = “boundless, unsated.”

line_details.greek: κυανόχρως, ἀδάμαστε, παναίολος, αἰολόμορφε,
line_details.english: dark-blue in hue, indomitable, all-variegated, changeful of form,
line_details.note: κυανόχρως = “dark‑blue/azure‑hued”; παναίολος = “all‑variegated, dappled”; αἰολόμορφος = “changeful in form.”

line_details.greek: πανδερκές, Κρονότεκνε, μάκαρ, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον,
line_details.english: all-seeing, child of Kronos, blessed, most-exalted daimon,
line_details.note: Κρονότεκνε literally “child of Kronos”; in Orphic contexts Kronos can also stand for Chronos (Time). δαῖμον denotes a divine power, not a malign “demon.”

line_details.greek: κλῦθ’ ἐπάγων ζωὴν ὁσίην μύστῃ νεοφάντῃ.
line_details.english: hear, and bring holy life to the newly revealed mystes.
line_details.note: νεοφάντῃ (“newly‑manifest”) modifies μύστῃ (“initiate”); the closing prayer asks the god to grant a holy/pious life to the neophyte.

text.english: O you who hold the ever-unwearied might of Zeus of the lofty halls, the portion allotted to the stars, to Helios, and to Selene, all-subduer, fire-breathing, the spark for all living beings, high-shining Aither, the best element of the cosmos, O splendid offspring, bearer of brilliance, star-gleaming, calling upon you I beseech that you be well-tempered and serene.
text.greek: Ὦ Διὸς ὑψιμέλαθρον ἔχων κράτος αἰὲν ἀτειρές, ἄστρων ἠελίου τε σεληναίης τε μέρισμα, πανδαμάτωρ, πυρίπνους, πᾶσιν ζῳοῖσιν ἔναυσμα, ὑψιφανὴς Αἰθήρ, κόσμου στοιχεῖον ἄριστον · ἀγλαὸν ὦ βλάστημα, σελασφόρον, ἀστεροφεγγές, κικλήσκων λίτομαί σε, κεκραμένον εὔδιον εἶναι.

line_details.greek: Ὦ Διὸς ὑψιμέλαθρον ἔχων κράτος αἰὲν ἀτειρές,
line_details.english: O you who hold the ever-unwearied might of Zeus of the lofty halls,
line_details.note: ὑψιμέλαθρον (“of lofty halls”): an epithet associated with Zeus; the syntax allows a transferred epithet to κράτος; αἰὲν ἀτειρές = “ever indomitable/unyielding.”

line_details.greek: ἄστρων ἠελίου τε σεληναίης τε μέρισμα,
line_details.english: the portion allotted to the stars, to Helios, and to Selene,
line_details.note: μέρισμα = “allotment/portion,” here the cosmic region assigned to heavenly bodies; Helios and Selene are preserved as theonyms.

line_details.greek: πανδαμάτωρ, πυρίπνους, πᾶσιν ζῳοῖσιν ἔναυσμα,
line_details.english: all-subduer, fire-breathing, the spark for all living beings,
line_details.note: πανδαμάτωρ = “all-subduer/all-tamer” (epic); πυρίπνους = “fire-breathing/fiery-breathing”; ἔναυσμα = “kindling/spark,” source of vital ignition for life.

line_details.greek: ὑψιφανὴς Αἰθήρ, κόσμου στοιχεῖον ἄριστον
line_details.english: high-shining Aither, the best element of the cosmos,
line_details.note: ὑψιφανής = “high-shining”; στοιχεῖον = “element” in later/technical sense; ἄριστον = “best/noblest,” asserting Aither’s primacy among elements.
The mid-dot (·) marks a major pause/colon in the Greek; no lexical content to translate.

line_details.greek: ἀγλαὸν ὦ βλάστημα, σελασφόρον, ἀστεροφεγγές,
line_details.english: O splendid offspring, bearer of brilliance, star-gleaming,
line_details.note: βλάστημα literally “shoot/sprout,” here “offspring” in a cosmic-genealogical sense; σελασφόρον = “brightness-bearing”; ἀστεροφεγγές = “star-shining.”

line_details.greek: κικλήσκων λίτομαί σε, κεκραμένον εὔδιον εἶναι.
line_details.english: calling upon you I beseech that you be well-tempered and serene.
line_details.note: κικλήσκων = “calling upon”; κεκραμένον (from κεράννυμι) = “well-mixed/tempered,” often of air; εὔδιον = “fair-weather/serene.” The prayer asks for benevolent, calm conditions.

text.english: Protogonos I call, two‑natured, great, aether‑wandering, egg‑born, exulting in golden pinions, bull‑eyed, the origin of the blessed and of mortal men; the seed much‑remembered, rich in orgia, Erikepaios, unspeakable, hidden, whirring‑sounding, all‑shining shoot, who by your eyes dispelled the murky mist of darkness, whirled everywhere by the gusts of your wings through the ordered world, bringing bright, holy light, whence I invoke you as Phanês, and as lord Priêpos, and as Antaugê of the circling gaze.
text.greek: Πρωτογόνον καλέω διφυῆ, μέγαν, αἰθερόπλαγκτον, ὠογενῆ, χρυσέησιν ἀγαλλόμενον πτερύγεσσιν, ταυρωπόν, γένεσιν μακάρων θνητῶν τ’ ἀνθρώπων · σπέρμα πολύμνηστον, πολυόργιον, Ἠρικεπαῖον, ἄρρητον, κρύφιον. ῥοιζήτορα, παμφαὲς ἔρνος · ὄσσων ὃς σκοτόεσσαν ἀπημαύρωσας ὁμίχλην, πάντῃ δινηθεὶς πτερύγων ῥιπαῖς κατὰ κόσμον · λαμπρὸ ν ἄγων φάος ἁγνόν, ἀφ’ οὗ σε Φάνητα κικλήσκω, ἠδὲ Πρίηπον ἄνακτα, καὶ Ἀνταύγην ἑλίκωπον.

line_details.greek: Πρωτογόνον καλέω διφυῆ, μέγαν, αἰθερόπλαγκτον,
line_details.english: Protogonos I call, two‑natured, great, aether‑wandering,
line_details.note: “two‑natured” (διφυής) in Orphic context suggests androgyny; “aether‑wandering” renders αἰθερόπλαγκτος.

line_details.greek: ὠογενῆ, χρυσέησιν ἀγαλλόμενον πτερύγεσσιν,
line_details.english: egg‑born, exulting in golden pinions,
line_details.note: “egg‑born” (ὠογενής) alludes to the cosmic egg; “golden pinions” are traditional attributes of Phanês.

line_details.greek: ταυρωπόν, γένεσιν μακάρων θνητῶν τ’ ἀνθρώπων ·
line_details.english: bull‑eyed, the origin of the blessed and of mortal men;
line_details.note: “bull‑eyed” (ταυρωπός) is a traditional divine epithet; γένεσις here = “origin/source.”

line_details.greek: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον, πολυόργιον, Ἠρικεπαῖον,
line_details.english: the seed much‑remembered, rich in orgia, Erikepaios,
line_details.note: πολύμνηστον = “much‑remembered/famed”; πολυόργιον = “rich in orgia (secret rites)”; Ἠρικεπαῖος (Erikepaios) is an obscure Orphic epithet/name retained by transliteration.

line_details.greek: ἄρρητον, κρύφιον. ῥοιζήτορα, παμφαὲς ἔρνος ·
line_details.english: unspeakable, hidden, whirring‑sounding, all‑shining shoot,
line_details.note: ῥοιζήτορα conveys a rushing/whirring sound; ἔρνος = “shoot, scion,” of cosmic generation.

line_details.greek: ὄσσων ὃς σκοτόεσσαν ἀπημαύρωσας ὁμίχλην,
line_details.english: who by your eyes dispelled the murky mist of darkness,
line_details.note: ὄσσων (genitive plural “of eyes”) functions instrumentally: “by your eyes”; ἀπημαύρωσας = “you dispelled/banished.”

line_details.greek: πάντῃ δινηθεὶς πτερύγων ῥιπαῖς κατὰ κόσμον ·
line_details.english: whirled everywhere by the gusts of your wings through the ordered world,
line_details.note: δινηθείς = “eddying/whirled”; κατὰ κόσμον can mean “through the cosmos” or “in due order.”

line_details.greek: λαμπρὸ ν ἄγων φάος ἁγνόν, ἀφ’ οὗ σε Φάνητα κικλήσκω,
line_details.english: bringing bright, holy light, whence I invoke you as Phanês,
line_details.note: Φάνητα (Phanês) from φαίνω, “to bring to light”; the name emphasizes his role as revealer of light.

line_details.greek: ἠδὲ Πρίηπον ἄνακτα, καὶ Ἀνταύγην ἑλίκωπον.
line_details.english: and as lord Priêpos, and as Antaugê of the circling gaze.
line_details.note: Πρίηπος (Priêpos) is the Orphic form of Priapos; Ἀνταύγη (Antaugê, “Reflected‑Gleam”) is a by‑name of Phanês; ἑλίκωπος = “with circling/rolling gaze.”

text.english: But come, blessed one, of much counsel, rich in seed, step rejoicing into the holy, many‑patterned rite for the revealers of the orgia.
text.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πολύμητι, πολύσπορε, βαῖνε γεγηθὼς ἐς τελετ ὴν ἁγίην πολυποίκιλον ὀργιοφάνταις.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πολύμητι, πολύσπορε, βαῖνε γεγηθὼς
line_details.english: But come, blessed one, of much counsel, rich in seed, step rejoicing
line_details.note: πολύμητις = “of much counsel, resourceful”; πολύσπορος = “rich in seed, much‑sowing”; βαῖνε is the hymnic “come/step.”

line_details.greek: ἐς τελετ ὴν ἁγίην πολυποίκιλον ὀργιοφάνταις.
line_details.english: into the holy, many‑patterned rite for the revealers of the orgia.
line_details.note: τελετή = initiation‑rite; πολυποίκιλος = “many‑patterned/variegated”; ὀργιοφάνταις = “to the revealers of the orgia (mysteries).”

text.english: I summon forth the sacred radiance of the heavenly stars, calling upon pure daimones with holy-sacrificial voices, Heavenly Stars, dear children of black Nyx, enthroned round about, wheeling in encircling eddies, gleaming back, fiery, ever the begetters of all things; fate-dealing, being indicators of every allotment; guiding the divine path of mortal men; wearing seven-lumined zones, wandering through the mist; both heavenly and chthonian, fire-running, ever-unwearied, ever lighting up Night’s gloom-like veil, shining with sparkles, kindly and nocturnal; come to the well-hallowed rite, to its much-instructive labors, noble, completing your course for illustrious works.
text.greek: Ἄστρων οὐρανίων ἱερὸν σέλας ἐκπροκαλο ῦμαι, εὐιέραις φωνῇ σι κικλήσκων δαίμονας ἁγνούς. Ἀστέρες οὐράνιοι, Νυκτὸς φίλα τέκνα μελαίνης, ἐγκυκλίοις δίν ῃσι περιθρόνιοι κυκλέοντες. ἀνταυγε ῖς, πυρόεντες, ἀεὶ γενετ ῆρες ἁπάντων· μοιρίδιοι, πάσης μοίρης σημάντορες ὄντες · θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων θείην διέποντες ἀταρπόν · ἑπταφαε ῖς ζώνας ἐφορώμενοι, ἠερόπλαγκτοι· οὐράνιοι χθόνιοί τε, πυρίδρομοι, αἰὲν ἀτειρε ῖς αὐγάξοντες ἀεὶ νυκτὸς ζοφοειδέα πέπλον, μαρμαρυγαῖς στίλβοντες, ἐΰφρονες ἐννύχιοί τε · ἔλθετ’ ἐπ’ εὐιέρου τελετῆς πολυΐστορας ἄθλους, ἐσθλο ὶ ἐπ’ εὐδόξοις ἔργοις δρόμον ἐκτελέοντες.

line_details.greek: Ἄστρων οὐρανίων ἱερὸν σέλας ἐκπροκαλο ῦμαι,
line_details.english: I summon forth the sacred radiance of the heavenly stars,
line_details.note: ἐκπροκαλοῦμαι intensifies the invocation (“call forth”); σέλας = “radiance” of the stars. The spacing in ἐκπροκαλοῦμαι in the source is typographical.

line_details.greek: εὐιέραις φωνῇ σι κικλήσκων δαίμονας ἁγνούς.
line_details.english: calling upon pure daimones with holy-sacrificial voices,
line_details.note: εὐιέραις (“of good sacrifice,” hence “holy”) marks ritual diction; φωνῇσι is epic dative plural. Δαίμονες here means “divine powers,” not “demons.” The spacing in “σι κικλήσκων” is typographical.

line_details.greek: Ἀστέρες οὐράνιοι, Νυκτὸς φίλα τέκνα μελαίνης,
line_details.english: Heavenly Stars, dear children of black Nyx,
line_details.note: Nyx is the goddess of Night; μελαίνη (“black”) is a conventional cultic epithet.

line_details.greek: ἐγκυκλίοις δίν ῃσι περιθρόνιοι κυκλέοντες.
line_details.english: enthroned round about, wheeling in encircling eddies,
line_details.note: περιθρόνιοι (“around the throne”) likely refers to encircling the celestial pole or divine throne; ἐγκυκλίοις δίναισι (“in encircling vortices”) evokes cosmic rotation. The spacing in δίναισι is typographical.

line_details.greek: ἀνταυγε ῖς, πυρόεντες, ἀεὶ γενετ ῆρες ἁπάντων·
line_details.english: gleaming back, fiery, ever the begetters of all things;
line_details.note: ἀνταυγεῖς can suggest “gleaming back” (often of reflected light); γενετῆρες (“begetters”) points to the stars’ generative/cosmic influence. Spacing in ἀνταυγεῖς and γενετῆρες is typographical.

line_details.greek: μοιρίδιοι, πάσης μοίρης σημάντορες ὄντες ·
line_details.english: fate-dealing, being indicators of every allotment;
line_details.note: μοιρίδιοι (“belonging to Moira,” hence “fate-dealing”); σημάντορες (“indicators, sign-givers”) presents the stars as signs of destiny (astrological nuance).

line_details.greek: θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων θείην διέποντες ἀταρπόν ·
line_details.english: guiding the divine path of mortal men;
line_details.note: θείην ἀταρπόν (“divine path”) can denote both destiny and the navigational/astrological course governed by the stars.

line_details.greek: ἑπταφαε ῖς ζώνας ἐφορώμενοι, ἠερόπλαγκτοι·
line_details.english: wearing seven-lumined zones, wandering through the mist;
line_details.note: ἑπταφαεῖς ζώνας (“seven-lumined zones”) probably the seven planetary circles or belts of the sky; ἠερόπλαγκτοι = “wandering through the mist.”

line_details.greek: οὐράνιοι χθόνιοί τε, πυρίδρομοι, αἰὲν ἀτειρε ῖς
line_details.english: both heavenly and chthonian, fire-running, ever-unwearied,
line_details.note: οὐράνιοι χθόνιοί τε (“both heavenly and chthonian”) because they rise and set; πυρίδρομοι = “fire-running”; ἀτειρεῖς = “unwearied/unyielding.” Spacing in ἀτειρεῖς is typographical.

line_details.greek: αὐγάξοντες ἀεὶ νυκτὸς ζοφοειδέα πέπλον,
line_details.english: ever lighting up Night’s gloom-like veil,
line_details.note: ζοφοειδές πέπλον (“gloom-like veil”) is a standard image for Night; αὐγάξοντες = “giving light, illuminating.”

line_details.greek: μαρμαρυγαῖς στίλβοντες, ἐΰφρονες ἐννύχιοί τε ·
line_details.english: shining with sparkles, kindly and nocturnal;
line_details.note: μαρμαρυγαί = “sparkles, flickers”; ἐύφρονες (“kindly, benevolent”); ἐννύχιοι (“of the night, nocturnal”).

line_details.greek: ἔλθετ’ ἐπ’ εὐιέρου τελετῆς πολυΐστορας ἄθλους,
line_details.english: come to the well-hallowed rite, to its much-instructive labors,
line_details.note: πολυΐστορας ἄθλους is difficult: either “much-instructive labors” of the rite or “widely-witnessed toils.” The translation adopts the former; many take πολυΐστορας as modifying ἄθλους.

line_details.greek: ἐσθλο ὶ ἐπ’ εὐδόξοις ἔργοις δρόμον ἐκτελέοντες.
line_details.english: noble, completing your course for illustrious works.
line_details.note: δρόμον ἐκτελέοντες (“completing your course”) suits celestial motion; ἐπ’ εὐδόξοις ἔργοις (“for illustrious works”) likely refers to the honored outcomes of the rite.

text.english: Hear, blessed one, having the all-seeing, eternal eye, Titan of golden brightness, Hyperiōn, celestial light, self-born, untiring, the sweet countenance of living beings, right-hand begetter of Dawn, left-hand of Night, holding the mingling of the seasons, dancing with four-stepping feet, swift-running, whirring, fiery, bright-faced, charioteer, driving your course by the eddies of the boundless whorl, guide to good for the pious, mighty against the impious, golden-lyred, drawing the harmonious course of the cosmos, sign-giver of good things, season-nurturing youth, world-ruler, whistler, fire-runner, spiral-wheeling one, light-bringer, displayer of shifting signs, life-bringer, fruitful Paian, sootless, undefiled, father of Time, immortal Zeus, giver of fair weather, all-shining, the world’s encircling eye, both setting and shining with lovely, radiant rays, index of justice, lover of streams, lord of the cosmos, trusty guardian, ever most high, helper to all, eye of justice, light of life; O driver of horses, with shrill whip urging on your four-horsed chariot, hear my words, and show forth a sweet life to the initiates.
text.greek: Κλῦθι μάκαρ, πανδερκὲς ἔχων αἰώνιον ὄμμα, Τιτ ὰν χρυσαυγής, ὑπερίων, οὐράνιον φῶς· αὐτοφυής, ἀκάμας, ζώων ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι· δεξι ὲ μὲν γενέτωρ ἠοῦς, εὐώνυμε νυκτός· κρᾶσιν ἔχων ὡρῶν, τετραβάμοσι ποσσὶ χορεύων. εὔδρομε, ῥοιζήτωρ, πυρόεις, φαιδρωπέ, διφρευτά, ῥόμβου ἀπειρεσίου δινεύμασιν οἶμον ἐλαύνων· εὐσεβέσιν καθοδηγὲ καλῶν, ζαμενὴ ς ἀσεβο ῦσιν. χρησολύρη, κόσμου τὸν ἐναρμόνιον δρόμον ἕλκων · ἔργων σημάντωρ ἀγαθῶ ν, ὡροτρόφε κοῦρε. κοσμοκράτωρ, συρικτά, πυρίδρομε, κυκλοέλικτε, φωσφόρος, α ἰολόδεικτα, φερέσβιε, κάρπιμε Παιάν· ἀϊθαλής, ἀμίαντε, χρόνου πάτερ, ἀθάνατε Ζεῦ, εὔδιε, πασιφαής, κόσμου τὸ περίδρομον ὄμμα, σβεννύμενον λάμπων τε καλαῖς ἀκτῖσι φαεινα ῖς· δεῖκτα δικαιοσύνης, φιλονάματε, δέσποτα κόσμου· πιστοφύλαξ, αἰεὶ πανυπέρτατε, πᾶσιν ἀρωγέ · ὄμμα δικαιοσύνης, ζωῆς φ ῶς· ὦ ἐλάσιππε, μάστιγι λιγυρ ῇ τετράορον ἅρμα διώκων, κλῦθι λόγων, ἡδὺν δὲ βίον μύστῃ σι πρόφαινε.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθι μάκαρ, πανδερκὲς ἔχων αἰώνιον ὄμμα,
line_details.english: Hear, blessed one, having the all-seeing, eternal eye,
line_details.note: πανδερκής literally “all-seeing”; αἰώνιον ὄμμα “eternal eye” is a standard solar epithet.

line_details.greek: Τιτ ὰν χρυσαυγής, ὑπερίων , οὐράνιον φῶς·
line_details.english: Titan of golden brightness, Hyperiōn, celestial light,
line_details.note: Read Τιτάν χρυσαυγής, Ὑπερίων; Hyperiōn is a solar theonym; χρυσαυγής = “golden-rayed/bright.”

line_details.greek: αὐτοφυής, ἀκάμας, ζώων ἡδεῖα πρόσοψι·
line_details.english: self-born, untiring, the sweet countenance of living beings,
line_details.note: αὐτοφυής “self-generated,” ἀκάμας “untiring”; πρόσοψις here “aspect/face,” hence “sweet to the sight of living beings.”

line_details.greek: δεξι ὲ μὲν γενέτωρ ἠοῦς, εὐώνυμε νυκτός·
line_details.english: right-hand begetter of Dawn, left-hand of Night,
line_details.note: εὐώνυμος is the euphemistic “left(-handed)”; the line marks the Sun’s position relative to Dawn and Night.

line_details.greek: κρᾶσιν ἔχων ὡρῶν, τετραβάμοσι ποσσὶ χορεύων.
line_details.english: holding the mingling of the seasons, dancing with four-stepping feet,
line_details.note: κρᾶσις ὡρῶν = “mixing of seasons”; “four-stepping feet” alludes to the four seasons.

line_details.greek: εὔδρομε, ῥοιζήτωρ, πυρόεις, φαιδρωπέ, διφρευτά,
line_details.english: swift-running, whirring, fiery, bright-faced, charioteer,
line_details.note: ῥοιζητήρ/ῥοιζήτωρ = “one who makes a whirring noise”; διφρευτής “charioteer.”

line_details.greek: ῥόμβου ἀπειρεσίου δινεύμασιν οἶμον ἐλαύνων·
line_details.english: driving your course by the eddies of the boundless whorl,
line_details.note: ῥόμβος is a “whorl/bull-roarer”; here the cosmic whorl, i.e., the revolving sphere; δινεύματα “eddies, gyrations.”

line_details.greek: εὐσεβέσιν καθοδηγὲ καλῶν, ζαμενὴ ς ἀσεβο ῦσιν.
line_details.english: guide to good for the pious, mighty against the impious,
line_details.note: ζαμενής = “mighty/vehement”; thus benevolent to the pious, formidable to the impious.

line_details.greek: χρησολύρη, κόσμου τὸν ἐναρμόνιον δρόμον ἕλκων ·
line_details.english: golden-lyred, drawing the harmonious course of the cosmos,
line_details.note: χρυσολύρη “golden-lyred” evokes Apollo; Orphic syncretism blends Hēlios–Apollo; ἐναρμόνιος “harmonious” (cosmic harmony).

line_details.greek: ἔργων σημάντωρ ἀγαθῶ ν, ὡροτρόφε κοῦρε.
line_details.english: sign-giver of good things, season-nurturing youth,
line_details.note: σημάντωρ “sign-giver/revealer”; ὡροτρόφος “nourisher of the hours/seasons”; κοῦρος “youth.”

line_details.greek: κοσμοκράτωρ, συρικτά, πυρίδρομε, κυκλοέλικτε,
line_details.english: world-ruler, whistler, fire-runner, spiral-wheeling one,
line_details.note: συρικτά “whistler/piper” (uncertain nuance); πυρίδρομος “fire-runner”; κυκλοέλικτος “coiling/spiralling in circles,” of the solar path.

line_details.greek: φωσφόρος, α ἰολόδεικτα, φερέσβιε, κάρπιμε Παιάν·
line_details.english: light-bringer, displayer of shifting signs, life-bringer, fruitful Paian,
line_details.note: αἰολόδεικτος “showing variegated/shifting signs” (aiolos = changeful); φερέσβιος “life-bringing”; Παιάν = Paiān (Apollo).

line_details.greek: ἀϊθαλής, ἀμίαντε, χρόνου πάτερ, ἀθάνατε Ζεῦ,
line_details.english: sootless, undefiled, father of Time, immortal Zeus,
line_details.note: ἀϊθαλής with diaeresis = “unsooty, clean-burning”; χρόνου πάτερ “father of Time” reflects Orphic Zeus–Aion/Helios syncretism.

line_details.greek: εὔδιε, πασιφαής, κόσμου τὸ περίδρομον ὄμμα,
line_details.english: giver of fair weather, all-shining, the world’s encircling eye,
line_details.note: εὔδιος “fair-weathering”; περίδρομον ὄμμα “the encircling eye” = the Sun as the world’s eye.

line_details.greek: σβεννύμενον λάμπων τε καλαῖς ἀκτῖσι φαεινα ῖς·
line_details.english: both setting and shining with lovely, radiant rays,
line_details.note: σβεννύμενον … λάμπων paradoxically expresses setting and shining (rising) with beautiful rays.

line_details.greek: δεῖκτα δικαιοσύνης, φιλονάματε, δέσποτα κόσμου·
line_details.english: index of justice, lover of streams, lord of the cosmos,
line_details.note: δεῖκτα (sc. δείκτης) “indicator” of justice; φιλονάματος “lover of streams” (νάμα = stream), perhaps of the Sun’s horse-baths.

line_details.greek: πιστοφύλαξ, αἰεὶ πανυπέρτατε, πᾶσιν ἀρωγέ ·
line_details.english: trusty guardian, ever most high, helper to all,
line_details.note: πιστοφύλαξ “faithful guardian”; πανυπέρτατος superlative “most supreme”; ἀρωγός “helper.”

line_details.greek: ὄμμα δικαιοσύνης, ζωῆς φ ῶς· ὦ ἐλάσιππε,
line_details.english: eye of justice, light of life; O driver of horses,
line_details.note: Repetition of the justice motif; ἐλάσιππος “horse-driver.”

line_details.greek: μάστιγι λιγυρ ῇ τετράορον ἅρμα διώκων,
line_details.english: with shrill whip urging on your four-horsed chariot,
line_details.note: τετράορον ἅρμα is an Orphic form meaning “four-horsed chariot” (cf. more common τέθριππον).

line_details.greek: κλῦθι λόγων, ἡδὺν δὲ βίον μύστῃ σι πρόφαινε.
line_details.english: hear my words, and show forth a sweet life to the initiates.
line_details.note: μύστῃσι is dative plural “to the initiates”; πρόφαινε “manifest/show forth”—a typical Orphic closing petition.

text.english: Hear, O queenly goddess, light-bringer, divine Selene; bull-horned Mene, night-roaming, air-wandering; nocturnal one, torch-bearer, maiden, well-starred Mene; waxing and waning, both female and male; bringer of radiance, horse-loving, mother of Time, fruit-bearing; amber-bright, grave of heart, she who beams down, helper in childbirth; all-seeing, lover of wakefulness, abounding in fair stars; rejoicing in stillness and in the kindly night of blessed lot; shining one, grace-bestowing, bringer-to-fulfillment, ornament of the night; ruler of the stars, long-robed, of winding course, all-wise maiden, come, blessed one, gracious, well-starred, with your own radiance, shining, and saving your young suppliants, O maiden.
text.greek: Κλῦθι, θεὰ βασίλεια, φαεσφόρε, δῖα Σελήνη · ταυρόκερως Μήνη, νυκτιδρόμος, ἠεροφο ῖτι, ἐννυχίη, δ ᾳδοῦχε, κόρη, εὐάστερε, Μήνη· αὐξομένη καὶ λειπομένη, θῆλύς τε καὶ ἄρσην· αὐγήτειρα, φίλιππε, χρόνου μῆτερ, φερέκαρπε· ἠλεκτρίς, βαρύθυμε, καταυγάστειρα, λοχείη· πανδερκής, φιλάγρυπνε, καλοῖς ἄστροισι βρύουσα· ἡσυχί ῃ χαίρουσα καὶ εὐφρόν ῃ ὀλβιομοίρ ῳ· λαμπετίη, χαριδῶτι, τελεσφόρε, νυκτὸς ἄγαλμα· ἀστράρχη, τανύπεπλ’, ἑ λικοδρόμε, πάνσοφε κούρη, ἐλθέ, μάκαιρ’, εὔφρων, εὐάστερε, φέγγεϊ τῷ σῷ λαμπ ομένη, σ ώζουσα νέους ἱκέτας σέο κούρη.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθι, θεὰ βασίλεια, φαεσφόρε, δῖα Σελήνη ·
line_details.english: Hear, O queenly goddess, light-bringer, divine Selene;
line_details.note: φαεσφόρε = “light-bringer”; θεὰ βασίλεια = “queenly goddess.” Retains the theonym Selene.

line_details.greek: ταυρόκερως Μήνη, νυκτιδρόμος, ἠεροφο ῖτι,
line_details.english: bull-horned Mene, night-roaming, air-wandering;
line_details.note: Μήνη (Mene) is a lunar theonym; ταυρόκερως “bull-horned” evokes the crescent; ἠεροφοῖτι = “air-wandering” (var. ἠεροφοίτη/ἠεροφοίτις).

line_details.greek: ἐννυχίη, δ ᾳδοῦχε , κόρη, εὐάστερε, Μήνη·
line_details.english: nocturnal one, torch-bearer, maiden, well-starred Mene;
line_details.note: ἐννυχίη = “nightly, nocturnal”; δᾳδοῦχε = “torch-bearer,” a ritual epithet; εὐάστερε = “well-starred.”

line_details.greek: αὐξομένη καὶ λειπομένη, θῆλύς τε καὶ ἄρσην·
line_details.english: waxing and waning, both female and male;
line_details.note: θῆλύς τε καὶ ἄρσην “female and male” marks the Moon’s androgynous/dual nature alongside its phases (waxing/waning).

line_details.greek: αὐγήτειρα , φίλιππε, χρόνου μῆτερ, φερέκαρπε·
line_details.english: bringer of radiance, horse-loving, mother of Time, fruit-bearing;
line_details.note: αὐγήτειρα “bringer of radiance/light”; φίλιππε “horse-loving” (chariot-imagery of lunar travel); χρόνου μῆτερ “mother of Time” (the Moon as measurer of time); φερέκαρπε “fruit-bearing” (fertility).

line_details.greek: ἠλεκτρίς, βαρύθυμε, καταυγάστειρα, λοχείη·
line_details.english: amber-bright, grave of heart, she who beams down, helper in childbirth;
line_details.note: ἠλεκτρίς relates to ἤλεκτρον “amber,” hence “amber-bright” (by extension “electric, radiant”); βαρύθυμε = “grave-minded”; καταυγάστειρα = “she who shines down”; λοχείη = “of/for childbirth.”

line_details.greek: πανδερκής, φιλάγρυπνε, καλοῖς ἄστροισι βρύουσα·
line_details.english: all-seeing, lover of wakefulness, abounding in fair stars;
line_details.note: φιλάγρυπνε = “lover of wakefulness” (friend to night-watchers); βρύουσα “teeming/abounding” with the fair stars of the night.

line_details.greek: ἡσυχί ῃ χαίρουσα καὶ εὐφρόν ῃ ὀλβιομοίρ ῳ·
line_details.english: rejoicing in stillness and in the kindly night of blessed lot;
line_details.note: εὐφρόνη here = “kindly night” (not the Grace Euphrosyne); ὀλβιομοίρῳ “of blessed lot,” dative with εὐφρόνη.

line_details.greek: λαμπετίη, χαριδῶτι, τελεσφόρε, νυκτὸς ἄγαλμα·
line_details.english: shining one, grace-bestowing, bringer-to-fulfillment, ornament of the night;
line_details.note: λαμπετίη “shining one” (cf. Lampetiê); τελεσφόρε “bringer to completion/fulfillment,” often with ritual nuance; νυκτὸς ἄγαλμα “ornament of night.”

line_details.greek: ἀστράρχη, τανύπεπλ’, ἑ λικοδρόμε, πάνσοφε κούρη,
line_details.english: ruler of the stars, long-robed, of winding course, all-wise maiden,
line_details.note: ἀστράρχη “ruler of the stars”; τανύπεπλος “long-robed”; ἑλικοδρόμε “of winding/spiraling course.”

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρ’, εὔφρων, εὐάστερε, φέγγεϊ τῷ σῷ
line_details.english: come, blessed one, gracious, well-starred, with your own radiance,
line_details.note: εὔφρων = “gracious, kindly”; εὐάστερε = “well-starred”; φέγγεϊ τῷ σῷ = “with your own radiance.”

line_details.greek: λαμπ ομένη, σ ώζουσα νέους ἱκέτας σέο κούρη.
line_details.english: shining, and saving your young suppliants, O maiden.
line_details.note: The participles λαμπομένη and σῴζουσα depend on “come” (ἐλθέ): “come … shining … and saving ….” Νέους ἱκέτας may mean “young” or “new/novice” suppliants.

text.english: O Physis, all-mother goddess, resourceful mother, heavenly, venerable, much-possessing daimon, queen; all-subduer, untamed, helmswoman, all-radiant, all-ruling, ever-honored, daimon most high; imperishable, first-born, of ancient fame, glory-bringing to mortals; nocturnal, much-experienced, light-bearing, awesomely enthroned, wheeling the noiseless trace with the ankle-bones of your feet; holy, orderer of the gods, and an end that is unending, common to all, yet alone sharing with none; self-sired, fatherless, male, of many counsels, greatest; fair-blooming, wreathed, friendly, much-mingled, knowing; leader, sovereign, life-bringing, all-nourishing maiden, Self-sufficiency, Dike; much-named Peitho of the Charites; aetherial, earthy, and ruling the sea; bitter to the base, yet sweet to those who obey; all-wise, all-giver, bringer, queen of all; nurturing growth, fertile, deliverer of what is ripened; of all you are father, mother, nurse, and wet-nurse; swift in childbed, blessed, much-seeding, of due season, impulse, all-skilled in crafts, shaper, much-possessing, mistress daimon, everlasting, movement-bearing, much-experienced, very prudent; whirling the swift current in an ever-flowing eddy; all-flowing, of circular form, subsisting in alien shapes; well-throned, honored, the only one accomplishing what has been decided; scepter-bearing from on high, heavy-roaring, mightiest; fearless, all-subduing, fate-ordained, Aisa, fire-breathing, everlasting life and immortal Providence.
text.greek: Ὦ Φύσι, παμμήτειρα θεά, πολυμήχανε μῆτερ, οὐρανίη, πρέσβειρα, πολύκτιτε δαῖμον, ἄνασσα · πανδαμάτωρ, ἀδάμαστε, κυβερνήτειρα, παναυγής, παντοκράτειρα, τιτιμέν’ ἀεί, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον· ἄφθιτε, πρωτογένεια, παλαίφατε, κυδιάνειρα· ἐννυχίη, πολύπειρε, σελασφόρε, δεινοκάθεκτε, ἄψοφον ἀστραγάλοισι ποδῶν ἴχνος εἱλίσσουσα· ἁγνή, κοσμήτειρα θεῶν, ἀτελής τε τελευτή, κοιν ὴ μὲν πάντεσσιν, ἀκοινώνητε δὲ μούνη· αὐτοπάτωρ, ἀπάτωρ, ἄρσην, πολύμητι, μεγίστη· εὐανθής, πλοκίη, φιλίη, πολύμικτε, δαῆμον· ἡγεμόνη, κράντειρα, φερέσβιε, παντρόφε κούρη, αὐτάρκεια, Δίκη· Χαρίτων πολυώνυμε πειθώ· αἰθερίη, χθονίη τε, καὶ εἰναλίη μεδέουσα· πικρ ὴ μέν φαύλοισι, γλυκεῖα δὲ πειθομένοισιν· πάνσοφε, πανδώτειρα, κομίστρια, παμβασίλεια· αὐξιτρόφος, πίειρα, πεπαινομένων τε λύτειρα· πάντων μὲν σὺ πατήρ, μήτηρ, τροφὸς ἠδὲ τιθηνός· ὠκυλόχεια, μάκαιρα, πολύσπορος, ὡριάς, ὁρμή, παντοτεχνές, πλάστειρα, πολύκτιτε, πότνιε δα ῖμον, ἀϊδίη, κινησιφόρος, πολύπειρε, περίφρων· ἀενά ῳ στροφάλιγγι θοὸν ῥύμα δινεύουσα· πάνρυτε, κυκλοτερής, ἀλλοτριομορφοδίαιτε· εὔθρονε, τιμήεσσα, μόνη τὸ κριθὲν τελέουσα, σκηπτούχοῦς’ ἐφύπερθε, βαρυβρεμέτειρα, κρατίστη· ἄτρομε, πανδαμάτειρα, πεπρωμένη, αἶσα, πυρίπνους ἀΐδιος ζωή, ἠδ’ ἀθανάτη τε πρόνοια.

line_details.greek: Ὦ Φύσι, παμμήτειρα θεά, πολυμήχανε μῆτερ,
line_details.english: O Physis, all-mother goddess, resourceful mother,
line_details.note: Φύσι is the vocative of Physis (“Nature”); παμμήτειρα = “all‑mother,” πολυμήχανε = “resourceful, of many devices.”

line_details.greek: οὐρανίη , πρέσβειρα, πολύκτιτε δαῖμον, ἄνασσα ·
line_details.english: heavenly, venerable, much-possessing daimon, queen;
line_details.note: πρέσβειρα = “venerable/elder”; πολύκτιτε = “much‑possessing, rich in possessions.”

line_details.greek: πανδαμάτωρ, ἀδάμαστε, κυβερνήτειρα, παναυγής,
line_details.english: all-subduer, untamed, helmswoman, all-radiant,
line_details.note: πανδαμάτωρ = “all‑subduer”; ἀδάμαστε = “untamed”; κυβερνήτειρα = fem. “helmswoman/steerswoman”; παναυγής = “all‑radiant.”

line_details.greek: παντοκράτειρα, τιτιμέν’ ἀεί, πανυπέρτατε δαῖμον·
line_details.english: all-ruling, ever-honored, daimon most high;
line_details.note: τιτιμέν’ ἀεί = “ever‑honored”; πανυπέρτατε = “most high/supreme” (voc. used of a fem. addressee).

line_details.greek: ἄφθιτε, πρωτογένεια, παλαίφατε, κυδιάνειρα·
line_details.english: imperishable, first-born, of ancient fame, glory-bringing to mortals;
line_details.note: πρωτογένεια = “first‑born”; παλαίφατε = “of ancient report/fame”; κυδιάνειρα = “glory‑bringing to men (mortals),” a traditional epic epithet.

line_details.greek: ἐννυχίη , πολύπειρε, σελασφόρε, δεινοκάθεκτε,
line_details.english: nocturnal, much-experienced, light-bearing, awesomely enthroned,
line_details.note: ἐννυχίη = “nocturnal”; πολύπειρε = “much‑experienced/skilled”; σελασφόρε = “light‑bearing”; δεινοκάθεκτε = “awesomely (terribly) enthroned.”

line_details.greek: ἄψοφον ἀστραγάλοισι ποδῶν ἴχνος εἱλίσσουσα·
line_details.english: wheeling the noiseless trace with the ankle-bones of your feet;
line_details.note: ἀστράγαλοι are the ankle‑bones; ἴχνος εἱλίσσειν “to coil/wheel a track,” an image for cosmic revolution.

line_details.greek: ἁγνή, κοσμήτειρα θεῶν, ἀτελής τε τελευτή,
line_details.english: holy, orderer of the gods, and an end that is unending,
line_details.note: κοσμήτειρα = “arranger/orderer”; ἀτελής τε τελευτή is paradoxical (“an end that is unending”), and τελευτή can also mean “initiation/consummation” in mystery vocabulary.

line_details.greek: κοιν ὴ μὲν πάντεσσιν, ἀκοινώνητε δὲ μούνη·
line_details.english: common to all, yet alone sharing with none;
line_details.note: Paradox of Nature as both universal and solitary: κοινή “common,” ἀκοινώνητος “sharing with none.”

line_details.greek: αὐτοπάτωρ, ἀπάτωρ, ἄρσην, πολύμητι, μεγίστη·
line_details.english: self-sired, fatherless, male, of many counsels, greatest;
line_details.note: αὐτοπάτωρ “self‑sired” with ἀπάτωρ “fatherless,” and ἄρσην “male”: deliberate androgynous/self‑caused paradox; πολύμητι = “of many counsels.”

line_details.greek: εὐανθής, πλοκίη, φιλίη , πολύμικτε, δαῆμον·
line_details.english: fair-blooming, wreathed, friendly, much-mingled, knowing;
line_details.note: πλοκίη = “plaited/wreathed/entwined”; δαῆμον is from δαήμων “knowing/skillful,” not δαίμων “daimon.”

line_details.greek: ἡγεμόνη, κράντειρα, φερέσβιε, παντρόφε κούρη,
line_details.english: leader, sovereign, life-bringing, all-nourishing maiden,
line_details.note: φερέσβιε = “life‑bringing/life‑sustaining”; κούρη “maiden” coexists with maternal roles, a typical hymnic tension.

line_details.greek: αὐτάρκεια, Δίκη· Χαρίτων πολυώνυμε πειθώ·
line_details.english: Self-sufficiency, Dike; much-named Peitho of the Charites;
line_details.note: Appositional theonyms: Dike (Justice) and Peitho (Persuasion) of the Charites (Graces).

line_details.greek: αἰθερίη, χθονίη τε, καὶ εἰναλίη μεδέουσα·
line_details.english: aetherial, earthy, and ruling the sea;
line_details.note: αἰθερίη = “aetherial, of the upper air”; εἰναλίη μεδέουσα = “ruling over the sea.”

line_details.greek: πικρ ὴ μέν φαύλοισι, γλυκεῖα δὲ πειθομένοισιν·
line_details.english: bitter to the base, yet sweet to those who obey;
line_details.note: φαῦλος = “base/worthless”; πειθόμενοι = “those who obey/are persuaded.”

line_details.greek: πάνσοφε, πανδώτειρα, κομίστρια, παμβασίλεια·
line_details.english: all-wise, all-giver, bringer, queen of all;
line_details.note: πανδώτειρα = “all‑giver”; κομίστρια = “bringer/conveyor”; παμβασίλεια = “queen of all.”

line_details.greek: αὐξιτρόφος, πίειρα, πεπαινομένων τε λύτειρα·
line_details.english: nurturing growth, fertile, deliverer of what is ripened;
line_details.note: αὐξιτρόφος = “growth‑nurturing”; πεπαινομένων from πεπαίνω “to ripen/soften”: hence “deliverer of what is ripened” (births, fruits).

line_details.greek: πάντων μὲν σὺ πατήρ, μήτηρ, τροφὸς ἠδὲ τιθηνός·
line_details.english: of all you are father, mother, nurse, and wet-nurse;
line_details.note: τροφός vs. τιθηνός: both “nurse,” with nuance of “feeder” vs. “wet‑nurse.”

line_details.greek: ὠκυλόχεια, μάκαιρα, πολύσπορος, ὡριάς, ὁρμή,
line_details.english: swift in childbed, blessed, much-seeding, of due season, impulse,
line_details.note: ὠκυλόχεια = “swift in childbirth”; πολύσπορος = “much‑seeded/very fruitful”; ὡριάς = “of due season”; ὁρμή = “impulse/prime drive.”

line_details.greek: παντοτεχνές, πλάστειρα, πολύκτιτε, πότνιε δα ῖμον,
line_details.english: all-skilled in crafts, shaper, much-possessing, mistress daimon,
line_details.note: παντοτεχνές = “skilled in every craft”; πλάστειρα = “shaper/molder.”

line_details.greek: ἀϊδίη, κινησιφόρος, πολύπειρε, περίφρων·
line_details.english: everlasting, movement-bearing, much-experienced, very prudent;
line_details.note: κινησιφόρος = “bearing movement” (source of motion); περίφρων = “very prudent/shrewd.”

line_details.greek: ἀενά ῳ στροφάλιγγι θοὸν ῥύμα δινεύουσα·
line_details.english: whirling the swift current in an ever-flowing eddy;
line_details.note: στροφάλιγξ = “whorl/eddy”; ῥῦμα = “current/flow”: cosmic vortex imagery.

line_details.greek: πάνρυτε, κυκλοτερής, ἀλλοτριομορφοδίαιτε·
line_details.english: all-flowing, of circular form, subsisting in alien shapes;
line_details.note: πανρυτε is a crux; commonly taken as “all‑flowing”; κυκλοτερής = “circular/round”; ἀλλοτριομορφοδίαιτος = “subsisting in alien forms” (inhabiting all shapes).

line_details.greek: εὔθρονε, τιμήεσσα, μόνη τὸ κριθὲν τελέουσα,
line_details.english: well-throned, honored, the only one accomplishing what has been decided;
line_details.note: εὔθρονος = “well‑throned”; τὸ κριθέν = “what has been judged/decided (by Fate).”

line_details.greek: σκηπτούχοῦς’ ἐφύπερθε, βαρυβρεμέτειρα, κρατίστη·
line_details.english: scepter-bearing from on high, heavy-roaring, mightiest;
line_details.note: σκηπτούχος = “scepter‑bearing”; βαρυβρεμέτειρα = “heavy‑roaring,” an epithet elsewhere of thunder‑gods, transferred to Physis.

line_details.greek: ἄτρομε, πανδαμάτειρα, πεπρωμένη, αἶσα, πυρίπνους
line_details.english: fearless, all-subduing, fate-ordained, Aisa, fire-breathing,
line_details.note: πεπρωμένη = “fate‑ordained”; Αἶσα (Aisa) = “Allotment/Fate”; πυρίπνους = “fire‑breathing,” suggesting elemental energy.

line_details.greek: ἀΐδιος ζωή, ἠδ’ ἀθανάτη τε πρόνοια.
line_details.english: everlasting life and immortal Providence.
line_details.note: πρόνοια = “Providence,” personified as an attribute of Physis.

text.english: You are all things; for you alone bring all these things to pass.
text.greek: πάντα σὺ ἔσσὶ · τὰ πάντα σὺ γὰρ μούνη τάδε τεύχεις.

line_details.greek: πάντα σὺ ἔσσὶ · τὰ πάντα σὺ γὰρ μούνη τάδε τεύχεις.
line_details.english: You are all things; for you alone bring all these things to pass.
line_details.note: τεύχεις = “bring about, effect.” Statement of monism: Physis is all things and the sole cause.

text.english: But, goddess, I entreat you, in prosperous seasons, to bring peace and health, and the increase of all things.
text.greek: ἀλλά, θεά, λίτομαί σε, σὺν εὐόλβοισιν ἐν ὥραις εἰρήνην ὑγίειανἄγειν, αὔξησιν ἁπάντων.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, θεά, λίτομαί σε, σὺν εὐόλβοισιν ἐν ὥραις
line_details.english: But, goddess, I entreat you, in prosperous seasons,
line_details.note: ὥραι = “seasons/appointed times”; εὐόλβοι = “prosperous, blessed.”

line_details.greek: εἰρήνην ὑγίειανἄγειν, αὔξησιν ἁπάντων.
line_details.english: to bring peace and health, and the increase of all things.
line_details.note: ἄγειν governs the objects of the prayer: “to bring” peace, health, and universal increase.

text.english: I call upon Pan, the mighty, the Pastoral One, the All of the cosmos, heaven and sea, and the all-sovereign earth, and immortal fire; for these are the members of Pan.
text.greek: Πᾶνα καλῶ κρατερόν, νόμιον, κόσμοιο τὸ σύμπαν, οὐρανὸν ἠδὲ θάλασσαν, ἰδὲ χθόνα παμβασίλειαν, καὶ πῦρ ἀθάνατον· τάδε γὰρ μέλη ἐστὶ τὰ Πανός.

line_details.greek: Πᾶνα καλῶ κρατερόν, νόμιον, κόσμοιο τὸ σύμπαν,
line_details.english: I call upon Pan, the mighty, the Pastoral One, the All of the cosmos,
line_details.note: “κόσμοιο τὸ σύμπαν” is appositional, playing on Pan’s name (“All”): Pan as the totality of the cosmos.

line_details.greek: οὐρανὸν ἠδὲ θάλασσαν, ἰδὲ χθόνα παμβασίλειαν,
line_details.english: heaven and sea, and the all-sovereign earth,
line_details.note: “παμβασίλειαν” = “all-sovereign,” an Orphic epithet of Earth’s universal rule.

line_details.greek: καὶ πῦρ ἀθάνατον· τάδε γὰρ μέλη ἐστὶ τὰ Πανός.
line_details.english: and immortal fire; for these are the members of Pan.
line_details.note: “μέλη” (“members/limbs”) presents the elements as Pan’s body in a cosmic-Pan theology.

text.english: Come, blessed one, leaper, all-ranging runner, co-throned with the Horai; goat-limbed, Bacchic reveler, lover of divine possession, star-dwelling; weaving the harmony of the cosmos with playful song, helper of visions, dread to mortal fears; rejoicing with goatherds by the springs and with cowherds, keen-sighted, hunter, friend of Echo, chorus-mate of the Nymphs; of every nature, begetter of all, many-named daimon; world-ruler, Increaser, Light-bringer, Fruitful Paian; cave-delighting, heavy in wrath, the true horned Zeus.
text.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σκιρτητά, περίδρομε, σύνθρονος ὅραις· αἰγομελές, βακχευτά, φιλένθεος, ἀστροδίαιτε· ἁρμονίην κόσμοιο κρέκων φιλοπαίγμονι μολπῇ, φαντασιῶν ἐπαρωγέ, φόβων ἔκπαγλε βροτείων· αἰγονόμοις χαίρων ἀνὰ πίδακας ἠδέ τε βούταις, εὔσκοπε, θηρητήρ, Ἠχοῦς φίλε, σύγχορε νυμφῶ ν· παντοφυής, γενέτωρ πάντων, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον· κοσμοκράτωρ, αὐξητά, φαεσφόρε, κάρπιμε Παιάν· ἀντροχαρές, βαρύμηνις, ἀληθὴς Ζε ὺς ὁκεράστης.

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σκιρτητά, περίδρομε, σύνθρονος ὅραις·
line_details.english: Come, blessed one, leaper, all-ranging runner, co-throned with the Horai;
line_details.note: “σύνθρονος ὅραις”: literally “sharing a throne with the Seasons” (the Horai), situating Pan in cosmic order/time.

line_details.greek: αἰγομελές, βακχευτά, φιλένθεος, ἀστροδίαιτε·
line_details.english: goat-limbed, Bacchic reveler, lover of divine possession, star-dwelling;
line_details.note: “αἰγομελής” = “goat-limbed”; “φιλένθεος” here “lover of divine possession/enthusiasm”; “ἀστροδίαιτος” = “star-dwelling.”

line_details.greek: ἁρμονίην κόσμοιο κρέκων φιλοπαίγμονι μολπῇ,
line_details.english: weaving the harmony of the cosmos with playful song,
line_details.note: “κρέκων” = “weaving” (of song); “φιλοπαίγμονι” = “play-loving/playful,” underscoring Pan’s musical play.

line_details.greek: φαντασιῶν ἐπαρωγέ, φόβων ἔκπαγλε βροτείων·
line_details.english: helper of visions, dread to mortal fears;
line_details.note: “φαντασίαι” are visionary apparitions; “ἔκπαγλος” = “terrible/awful,” hence “dread to mortal fears.”

line_details.greek: αἰγονόμοις χαίρων ἀνὰ πίδακας ἠδέ τε βούταις,
line_details.english: rejoicing with goatherds by the springs and with cowherds,
line_details.note: “πίδακες” are natural springs; the line evokes Pan’s pastoral haunts with goatherds and cowherds.

line_details.greek: εὔσκοπε, θηρητήρ, Ἠχοῦς φίλε, σύγχορε νυμφῶ ν·
line_details.english: keen-sighted, hunter, friend of Echo, chorus-mate of the Nymphs;
line_details.note: “εὔσκοπος” = “keen-sighted”; “σύγχορος” = “chorus-mate/fellow dancer”; Ἠχώ (Echo) personified.

line_details.greek: παντοφυής, γενέτωρ πάντων, πολυώνυμε δαῖμον·
line_details.english: of every nature, begetter of all, many-named daimon;
line_details.note: “παντοφυής” can mean “of every kind/nature” or “of all growths”; translation reflects the polyvalence.

line_details.greek: κοσμοκράτωρ, αὐξητά, φαεσφόρε, κάρπιμε Παιάν·
line_details.english: world-ruler, Increaser, Light-bringer, Fruitful Paian;
line_details.note: “Παιάν” (Paian) is typically an epithet of Apollo as healer; its application to Pan here is syncretic. “αὐξητά” = “Increaser.”

line_details.greek: ἀντροχαρές, βαρύμηνις, ἀληθὴς Ζε ὺς ὁκεράστης.
line_details.english: cave-delighting, heavy in wrath, the true horned Zeus.
line_details.note: Textually debated: many read ἀληθὴς Ζεὺς κεραστής (“true horned Zeus”). Our “true horned Zeus” reflects Pan’s horned form and his assimilation to Zeus. “βαρύμηνις” = “weighty in wrath.”

text.english: For upon you the boundless expanse of earth is set firm, and the deep-flowing water of the untiring sea yields, and Okeanos, encircling, coils the earth round with his waters; and the airy portion of sustenance, the kindling for living beings, and, above the summit, the eye of the lightest fire.
text.greek: σοὶ γὰρ ἀπειρέσιον γαίης πέδον ἐστήρικται, εἴκει δ’ ἀκαμάτου πόντου τὸ βαθύ ῤῥοον ὕ δωρ, Ὠκεανός τε πέριξ ἐν ὕδασι γαῖαν ἑλίσσων· ἀέριόν τε μέρισμα τροφῆς, ζῳοῖσιν ἔναυσμα, καὶ κορυφ ῆς ἐφύπερθεν ἐλαφροτάτου πυρὸς ὄμμα.

line_details.greek: σοὶ γὰρ ἀπειρέσιον γαίης πέδον ἐστήρικται,
line_details.english: For upon you the boundless expanse of earth is set firm,
line_details.note: “ἐστήρικται” = “is set firm,” presenting Pan as the cosmic foundation/basis.

line_details.greek: εἴκει δ’ ἀκαμάτου πόντου τὸ βαθύ ῤῥοον ὕ δωρ,
line_details.english: and the deep-flowing water of the untiring sea yields,
line_details.note: No special difficulty; “βαθυῤῥοον” = “deep-flowing,” “ἀκάματος” = “untiring.”

line_details.greek: Ὠκεανός τε πέριξ ἐν ὕδασι γαῖαν ἑλίσσων·
line_details.english: and Okeanos, encircling, coils the earth round with his waters;
line_details.note: Okeanos as the encircling world-river, a standard cosmological image.

line_details.greek: ἀέριόν τε μέρισμα τροφῆς, ζῳοῖσιν ἔναυσμα,
line_details.english: and the airy portion of sustenance, the kindling for living beings,
line_details.note: “ἀέριον μέρισμα τροφῆς” = the airy allotment of nourishment (breath); “ἔναυσμα” = “kindling/spark” for life.

line_details.greek: καὶ κορυφ ῆς ἐφύπερθεν ἐλαφροτάτου πυρὸς ὄμμα.
line_details.english: and, above the summit, the eye of the lightest fire.
line_details.note: “the lightest fire” signifies aither; its “eye” is plausibly the Sun (or the aitherial luminaries).

text.english: For these divine realms move, manifoldly parted, at your commands; and you alter the natures of all things by your providences, feeding the race of humans and the boundless cosmos as well.
text.greek: βαίνει γὰρ τάδε θεῖα πολύκριτα σῇσιν ἐφετμα ῖς· ἀλλάσσεις δὲ φύσεις πάντων ταῖς σῇσι προνοίαις, βόσκων ἀνθρώπων γενεὴν κα τ’ ἀπείρονα κόσμον.

line_details.greek: βαίνει γὰρ τάδε θεῖα πολύκριτα σῇσιν ἐφετμα ῖς·
line_details.english: For these divine realms move, manifoldly parted, at your commands;
line_details.note: “πολύκριτα” likely “much-partitioned/finely distinguished,” referring to the ordered separations of the elements; “ἐφετμαί” = divine commands/behests.

line_details.greek: ἀλλάσσεις δὲ φύσεις πάντων ταῖς σῇσι προνοίαις,
line_details.english: and you alter the natures of all things by your providences,
line_details.note: “πρόνοιαι” = providential cares; Pan as a cosmic provident force who alters/adjusts natures.

line_details.greek: βόσκων ἀνθρώπων γενεὴν κα τ’ ἀπείρονα κόσμον.
line_details.english: feeding the race of humans and the boundless cosmos as well.
line_details.note: No special difficulty; “βόσκων” (“feeding”) keeps the pastoral image at a cosmic scale.

text.english: But come, blessed one, Bacchic reveler, lover of possession, upon the holy libations, and grant a good completion of life, sending forth the Pan-ic oistros to the bounds of the earth.
text.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, βακχευτά, φιλένθεε, βαῖν’ ἐπὶ λοιβα ῖς εὐιέροις· ἀγαθὴ ν δ’ ὄ πασον βιότοιο τελευτὴν, Πανικ ὸν ἐκπέμπων οἶστρον ἐπὶ τέρματα γαίης.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, βακχευτά, φιλένθεε, βαῖν’ ἐπὶ λοιβα ῖς
line_details.english: But come, blessed one, Bacchic reveler, lover of possession, upon the holy libations,
line_details.note: “βαῖν’” = imperative “come”; “εὐίερος” = “most holy/very holy.”

line_details.greek: εὐιέροις· ἀγαθὴ ν δ’ ὄ πασον βιότοιο τελευτὴν,
line_details.english: and grant a good completion of life,
line_details.note: “τελευτή” = “completion/ending” (of life), not necessarily negative.

line_details.greek: Πανικ ὸν ἐκπέμπων οἶστρον ἐπὶ τέρματα γαίης.
line_details.english: sending forth the Pan-ic oistros to the bounds of the earth.
line_details.note: “Πανικὸς οἶστρος” = “Panic goad/frenzy.” The prayer may imply directing that force outwards “to the ends of the earth,” i.e., away from the worshipers; the nuance is ambivalent in ritual context.

text.english: Herakles, storm-hearted, mighty of strength, valiant Titan, strong-handed, indomitable, abounding in mighty labors, of changeful form, father of Chronos, eternal and kindly, ineffable, fierce-spirited, much-invoked, almighty ruler; holding an all-potent heart, great might—archer and seer; all-devouring, begetter of all, most high beyond all, helper of all; you who for mortals checked the savage tribes, driving them away, yearning for Peace, child-nurturing, bright and honored; self-sprung, unwearied, the earth’s finest offshoot; flashing with primeval bolts, great-named daimon, who wear about your head Eos and black Nyx, traversing twelve labors from the risings to the settings; immortal, much-experienced, boundless, city-smiting; come, blessed one, bringing every charm that soothes diseases.
