line_details.greek: σὺν σῇ μητρὶ θεᾷ μελανηφόρῳ Ἴσιδι σεμνῇ,
line_details.english: with your mother the goddess, august Isis in her black robe,
line_details.note: Melanēphoros (“black‑clad”) is a cult epithet of Isis; her role as “mother” reflects Greco‑Egyptian syncretism with Demeter‑type figures.

line_details.greek: Αἰγύπτου παρὰ χεῦμα σὺν ἀμφιπόλοισι τιθήναις·
line_details.english: by Egypt’s flood, with nurse‑attendant handmaids;
line_details.note: Aigyptou cheuma (“Egypt’s flood”) refers to the Nile; amphipoloi “attendants” and tithēnai “nurses” denote Isis’s ministering handmaids.

line_details.greek: εὐμενέουσ’ ἔλθοις ἀγάθ' ἐκτελέουσ' ἐπ’ ἀέθλοις.
line_details.english: come graciously, fulfilling good things upon the rites.
line_details.note: Elthois (optative) expresses a prayerful wish, “may you come.” Aethlois (“labors/contests”) in hymnic/mystery context = ritual performances; “fulfill good things” is a conventional benediction.

text.english: Horai, daughters of Themis and lord Zeus, Eunomia and Dike, and richly-blest Eirene, vernal, meadow-maidens, many-flowered, holy, all-hued, much-scented in flowerlike breaths, Horai ever-blooming, circling, sweet-faced, arrayed in dewy robes of much-nurturing flowers, playmates of Persephone, when the Moirai and the Charites lead her up to the light with circling dances, showing favor to Zeus and to the fruit-bestowing Mother; come to the auspicious, holy rites for the newly-initiated, bringing on without reproach the well-fruited births of the seasons.
text.greek: Ὧραι, θυγατέρες Θέμιδος καὶ Ζηνὸς ἄνακτος, Εὐνομίη τε Δίκη τε, καὶ Εἰρήνη πολύολβε, εἰαριναί, λειμωνιάδες, πολυάνθεμοι, ἁγναί, παντόχροοι, πολύοδμοι ἐν ἀνθεμοειδέσι πνοιαῖς, Ὧραι ἀειθαλέες, περικυκλάδες, ἡδυπρόσωποι· πέπλους ἑννύμεναι δροσεροὺς ἀνθέων πολυθρέπτων, Περσεφόνης συμπαίκτορες, εὖτέ ἑ Μοῖραι καὶ Χάριτες κυκλίοισι χοροῖς πρ ὸς φ ῶς ἀνάγωσιν. Ζην ὶ χαριζόμεναι καὶ μητέρι καρπ οδοτείρ ῃ· ἔλθετ’ ἐπ’ εὐφήμους τελετὰς ὁσίας νεομύστοις, εὐκάρπους καιρῶν γενέσεις ἐπάγουσαι ἀμεμφ ῶς.

line_details.greek: Ὧραι, θυγατέρες Θέμιδος καὶ Ζηνὸς ἄνακτος,
line_details.english: Horai, daughters of Themis and lord Zeus,
line_details.note: Horai: the Seasons/Hours; “lord” renders anaktos, a cultic epithet of Zeus.

line_details.greek: Εὐνομίη τε Δίκη τε, καὶ Εἰρήνη πολύολβε,
line_details.english: Eunomia and Dike, and richly-blest Eirene,
line_details.note: The three named Horai (Eunomia, Dike, Eirene) follow Hesiod; poly-olbe = “richly-blest.”

line_details.greek: εἰαριναί, λειμωνιάδες, πολυάνθεμοι, ἁγναί,
line_details.english: vernal, meadow-maidens, many-flowered, holy,
line_details.note: eiarinai = “vernal”; leimoniades suggests nymph-like “meadow-maidens”; hagnai = “holy/pure.”

line_details.greek: παντόχροοι, πολύοδμοι ἐν ἀνθεμοειδέσι πνοιαῖς,
line_details.english: all-hued, much-scented in flowerlike breaths,
line_details.note: pantokhrooi = “all-hued” (from khrōs, “complexion/colour,” not from khronos, “time”); anthemoeidesi pnoiais literally “flower-like breaths/breezes,” i.e., fragrances.

line_details.greek: Ὧραι ἀειθαλέες, περικυκλάδες, ἡδυπρόσωποι·
line_details.english: Horai ever-blooming, circling, sweet-faced,
line_details.note: perikuklades is a rare epithet, “circling/all-circling,” evoking both round dances and the seasonal cycle (some MSS have similar forms like perikykl-).

line_details.greek: πέπλους ἑννύμεναι δροσεροὺς ἀνθέων πολυθρέπτων,
line_details.english: arrayed in dewy robes of much-nurturing flowers,
line_details.note: peplous hennymenai = “arrayed in robes”; anthēon polythreptōn may be active (“much-nurturing [to many]”) or passive (“much-nurtured”); I take it as active of flowers that feed many (e.g., bees, mortals).

line_details.greek: Περσεφόνης συμπαίκτορες, εὖτέ ἑ Μοῖραι
line_details.english: playmates of Persephone, when the Moirai
line_details.note: sympaiktores = “playmates”; eute he = “when (they) her,” with enclitic he referring to Persephone.

line_details.greek: καὶ Χάριτες κυκλίοισι χοροῖς πρ ὸς φ ῶς ἀνάγωσιν.
line_details.english: and the Charites lead her up to the light with circling dances,
line_details.note: Reading pros phōs anagōsin (“lead her up to the light”); kyklioisi khorois = “in circular dances.” (The spacing in the source is a typographical artifact.)

line_details.greek: Ζην ὶ χαριζόμεναι καὶ μητέρι καρπ οδοτείρ ῃ·
line_details.english: showing favor to Zeus and to the fruit-bestowing Mother;
line_details.note: kharizomenai = “showing favor to/pleasing”; “the fruit-bestowing Mother” is Demeter (Mētēr karpodoteira). (Spacing in source ‘karp-’ is accidental.)

line_details.greek: ἔλθετ’ ἐπ’ εὐφήμους τελετὰς ὁσίας νεομύστοις,
line_details.english: come to the auspicious, holy rites for the newly-initiated,
line_details.note: euphēmous in ritual contexts = “requiring/marked by auspicious silence”; teletai hosiai = “holy rites”; neomystois = “newly-initiated.”

line_details.greek: εὐκάρπους καιρῶν γενέσεις ἐπάγουσαι ἀμεμφ ῶς.
line_details.english: bringing on without reproach the well-fruited births of the seasons.
line_details.note: eukarpous geneseis = “well-fruited births/becomings”; kairōn = “of the seasons/appointed times”; amemphōs = “without reproach.” (Source spacing ‘amemph-’ is accidental.)

text.english: I invoke the Kadmeian maiden, the all-queen, fair-formed Semelê, lovely-tressed, deep-bosomed, mother of thyrsus-bearing Dionysos, much-rejoicing, who endured great birth-pangs beneath the fire-bearing ray, having borne by the counsels of immortal Zeus, the Kronian; having won honors from august Persephoneia, among mortal men throughout the trieteric seasons, whenever they perform the fruitful birth-pang of your Bakchos, both the well-holy table and the pure mysteries.
text.greek: Κικλήσκω κούρην Καδμη ΐδα παμβασίλειαν, εὐειδ ῆ Σεμέλην, ἐρατοπλόκαμον, βαθύκολπον, μητέρα θυρσοφόροιο Διωνύσου πολυγηθοῦς, ἣ μεγάλας ὠδῖνας ἐλάσσατο πυρφόρ ῳ αὐγῇ, ἀθανάτοιο τεκο ῦσα Διὸς βουλα ῖς Κρονίοιο· τιμ ὰς τευξαμένη παρ’ ἀγαυ ῆς Περσεφονείης ἐν θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἀνὰ τριετηρίδας ὥρας, ἡνίκα σο ῦ Βάκχου γονίμην ὠδῖνα τελ ῶσιν, εὐΐερόν τε τράπεζαν ἰδὲ μυστήριά θ’ ἁγνά.

line_details.greek: Κικλήσκω κούρην Καδμη ΐδα παμβασίλειαν,
line_details.english: I invoke the Kadmeian maiden, the all-queen,
line_details.note: Καδμηΐδα = “Kadmeian,” i.e., Theban (of Kadmos). Παμβασίλειαν literally “all-queen,” a typical Orphic superlative epithet.

line_details.greek: εὐειδ ῆ Σεμέλην, ἐρατοπλόκαμον, βαθύκολπον,
line_details.english: fair-formed Semelê, lovely-tressed, deep-bosomed,
line_details.note: Epic epithets: εὐειδής “fair-formed,” ἐρατοπλόκαμος “lovely-haired,” βαθύκολπος “deep-/full-bosomed.”

line_details.greek: μητέρα θυρσοφόροιο Διωνύσου πολυγηθοῦς,
line_details.english: mother of thyrsus-bearing Dionysos, much-rejoicing,
line_details.note: θυρσοφόρος “thyrsus-bearing” marks Dionysos’ cult; πολυγηθής “much-rejoicing,” an epithet of Bacchic joy.

line_details.greek: ἣ μεγάλας ὠδῖνας ἐλάσσατο πυρφόρ ῳ αὐγῇ,
line_details.english: who endured great birth-pangs beneath the fire-bearing ray,
line_details.note: πυρφόρῳ αὐγῇ “fire-bearing ray” alludes to Zeus’ lightning; ἐλάσσατο (mid.) “underwent/forced through” of labor-pangs.

line_details.greek: ἀθανάτοιο τεκο ῦσα Διὸς βουλα ῖς Κρονίοιο·
line_details.english: having borne by the counsels of immortal Zeus, the Kronian;
line_details.note: Διὸς βουλαῖς Κρονίοιο = “by the counsels of Kronian Zeus”; Κρόνιος is Zeus’ epithet (“son of Kronos”).

line_details.greek: τιμ ὰς τευξαμένη παρ’ ἀγαυ ῆς Περσεφονείης
line_details.english: having won honors from august Persephoneia,
line_details.note: τιμὰς τευξαμένη “having obtained honors” from Persephoneia hints at Semele’s posthumous deification (as Thyônê) in the Underworld.

line_details.greek: ἐν θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἀνὰ τριετηρίδας ὥρας,
line_details.english: among mortal men throughout the trieteric seasons,
line_details.note: τριετηρίδες “trieteric” refers to the (bi‑)annual/triennial Dionysiac festival cycle; θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσι is a pleonastic “among mortals.”

line_details.greek: ἡνίκα σο ῦ Βάκχου γονίμην ὠδῖνα τελ ῶσιν,
line_details.english: whenever they perform the fruitful birth-pang of your Bakchos,
line_details.note: γονίμην ὠδῖνα “fruitful birth-pang”: ritual reenactment of Semelê’s labor in Bacchic rites; “your Bakchos” = her son Dionysos.

line_details.greek: εὐΐερόν τε τράπεζαν ἰδὲ μυστήριά θ’ ἁγνά.
line_details.english: both the well-holy table and the pure mysteries.
line_details.note: εὐίερον “well-holy” (perhaps echoing the Bacchic cry euoi); τράπεζα “table” = cultic banquet; μυστήρια ἁγνά “pure mysteries.”

text.english: Now you, goddess, I beseech, Kadmeian maiden, queen, to be ever present, gentle of mind, for the initiates.
text.greek: νῦν σέ, θεά, λίτομαι, κούρη Καδμηῒς ἄνασσα, πρη ΰνοον καλέων αἰεὶ μύστῃσιν ὑπάρχειν.

line_details.greek: νῦν σέ, θεά, λίτομαι, κούρη Καδμηῒς ἄνασσα,
line_details.english: Now you, goddess, I beseech, Kadmeian maiden, queen,
line_details.note: Vocative accumulation heightens the prayer; “Kadmeian” again stresses Semelê’s Theban identity.

line_details.greek: πρη ΰνοον καλέων αἰεὶ μύστῃσιν ὑπάρχειν.
line_details.english: to be ever present, gentle of mind, for the initiates.
line_details.note: πρηΰνοον “gentle of mind, kindly-disposed”; ὑπάρχειν “be present/assist” is a conventional Orphic prayer ending; μύσται = initiates.

parts.part_title: Hymn to Dionysos Bassareus, of the Trieteric rite.

text.english: Come, blessed Dionysos, fire-sown, bull-browed, O Bassareus and Bakkhos, much-named, all-sovereign ruler, who delight in swords and in blood, and in holy Mainads; uttering the euai-cry through Olympus, loud-roaring, frenzied Bakkhos, thyrsus-armed, of heavy wrath, honored by all the gods and by mortal men, all who dwell upon the earth; come, blessed one, leaper, bringing abundant rejoicing to all.
text.greek: Ἐλθέ, μάκαρ Διόνυσε, πυρίσπορε, ταυρομέτωπε, Βάσσαρε καὶ Βακχε ῦ, πολυώνυμε, παντοδυνάστα, ὃς ξίφεσιν χαίρεις ἠδ’ αἵματι, Μαινάσι θ’ ἁγνα ῖς· εὐάζων κατ’ Ὄλυμπον, ἐρίβρομε, μαινόλα Βάκχε, θυρσεγχής, βαρύμηνι, τετιμένε πᾶσι θεοῖσιν καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν, ὅσοι χθόνα ναιετάουσιν· ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σκιρτητά, φέρων πολὺ γῆθος ἅπασιν.

line_details.greek: Ἐλθέ, μάκαρ Διόνυσε, πυρίσπορε, ταυρομέτωπε,
line_details.english: Come, blessed Dionysos, fire-sown, bull-browed,
line_details.note: πυρίσπορε literally “fire-sown” (often understood of Dionysos’ thunder/fire birth); ταυρομέτωπε = “bull-browed,” a standard Bacchic epithet.

line_details.greek: Βάσσαρε καὶ Βακχε ῦ, πολυώνυμε, παντοδυνάστα,
line_details.english: O Bassareus and Bakkhos, much-named, all-sovereign ruler,
line_details.note: Βάσσαρε is the Thracian epithet Bassareus (from the fox-skin, bassaris); Βακχεῦ is a vocative form related to Bakkhos (many mss. read Βάκχε). παντοδυνάστα = “all-powerful ruler.”

line_details.greek: ὃς ξίφεσιν χαίρεις ἠδ’ αἵματι, Μαινάσι θ’ ἁγνα ῖς·
line_details.english: who delight in swords and in blood, and in holy Mainads;
line_details.note: The delight “in swords and blood” evokes orgiastic/sacrificial aspects of Bacchic rites; Μαινάδες (“Mainads”) are his possessed female votaries, here called “holy.”

line_details.greek: εὐάζων κατ’ Ὄλυμπον, ἐρίβρομε, μαινόλα Βάκχε,
line_details.english: uttering the euai-cry through Olympus, loud-roaring, frenzied Bakkhos,
line_details.note: εὐάζων denotes the ritual cry euai/euoi; ἐρίβρομε = “loud-roaring”; μαινόλα = “raving, frenzied.”

line_details.greek: θυρσεγχής, βαρύμηνι, τετιμένε πᾶσι θεοῖσιν
line_details.english: thyrsus-armed, of heavy wrath, honored by all the gods
line_details.note: θυρσεγχής is “thyrsus-armed” (—εγχής ‘spear-wielding’ used with the thyrsus); βαρύμηνι = “of heavy wrath”; τετιμένε is passive “honored by.”

line_details.greek: καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν, ὅσοι χθόνα ναιετάουσιν·
line_details.english: and by mortal men, all who dwell upon the earth;
line_details.note: θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν is a pleonastic “mortal mortals,” intensifying universality; ναιετάουσιν = “dwell.”

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, σκιρτητά, φέρων πολὺ γῆθος ἅπασιν.
line_details.english: come, blessed one, leaper, bringing abundant rejoicing to all.
line_details.note: σκιρτητά = “leaper/dancer,” a Bacchic epithet; γῆθος = “gladness, rejoicing.”

text.english: I call upon Dionysos Liknitēs at these prayers, holy, both‑thriving, much‑desired, kindly Bakchos; beloved shoot of bridal chambers, and of well‑crowned Aphroditē, who once amid the woodlands you shook with your danced steps, with the graceful Nymphs, driven along by frenzies.
text.greek: Βικνίτην Διόνυσον ἐπ’ ευχα ῖς τα ῖσδε κικλήσκω, ȃύσιον, ἀμφιθαλ ῆ, πεποθημένον, εὔφρονα Ǻάκχον· νυμφέων ἔρνος ἐραστόν, ἐ Ȩστεφάνου τ’ ਝφροδίτης, ὅς ποτ’ ἀνὰ δρυμο ઃς κεχορευμένα βήματα πάλλες σઃν νύμφαις χαρίεσσιν, ἐλαυνόμενος μανί ૉσιν.

line_details.greek: Βικνίτην Διόνυσον ἐπ’ ευχα ῖς τα ῖσδε κικλήσκω,
line_details.english: I call upon Dionysos Liknitēs at these prayers,
line_details.note: Βικνίτην = Λικνίτην (Liknitēs), the epithet of Dionysos associated with the liknon (winnowing‑fan/cradle) used in his mysteries; I translate with the cult title preserved.

line_details.greek: ȃύσιον, ἀμφιθαλ ῆ, πεποθημένον, εὔφρονα Ǻάκχον·
line_details.english: holy, both‑thriving, much‑desired, kindly Bakchos;
line_details.note: The transmitted ȃύσιον is likely ἁγνίον/ἁγνόν (“holy”). ἀμφιθαλής can mean “having both parents alive” (apt for the divine child) or “flourishing on both sides,” a viticultural image; I render it as “both‑thriving.” “εὔφρων” in cultic address = “kindly/propitious.”

line_details.greek: νυμφέων ἔρνος ἐραστόν, ἐ Ȩστεφάνου τ’ ਝφροδίτης,
line_details.english: beloved shoot of bridal chambers, and of well‑crowned Aphroditē,
line_details.note: νυμφέων ἔρνος = “shoot/offshoot of bridal chambers,” a genealogical and fertility metaphor; ἐὖ/εὐ‑στεφάνου (“well‑crowned/garlanded”) modifies Aphroditē, highlighting festal adornment.

line_details.greek: ὅς ποτ’ ἀνὰ δρυμο ઃς κεχορευμένα βήματα πάλλες
line_details.english: who once amid the woodlands you shook with your danced steps,
line_details.note: κεχορευμένα βήματα πάλλεις is a vivid idiom: “you shake/brandish danced steps,” i.e., set dancing in motion; I keep the energetic metaphor of πάλλειν.

line_details.greek: σઃν νύμφαις χαρίεσσιν, ἐλαυνόμενος μανί ૉσιν.
line_details.english: with the graceful Nymphs, driven along by frenzies.
line_details.note: μανίαισιν (“frenzies”) is the Bacchic mania that drives the dance; Nymphs are Dionysiac companions.

text.english: and, by the counsels of Zeus, to proud Persephonē being borne, you were reared, dear to the immortal gods.
text.greek: καὶ βουλ ૌσι Διὸς πρ ὸς ἀγαυ ήν ĭερσεφόνειαν ἀχθε ὶς ἐȟετράφης, φίλος ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν.

line_details.greek: καὶ βουλ ૌσι Διὸς πρ ὸς ἀγαυ ήν ĭερσεφόνειαν
line_details.english: and, by the counsels of Zeus, to proud Persephonē
line_details.note: βουλαῖσι Διός… πρὸς ἀγαυὴν Περσεφόνειαν alludes to the Orphic myth in which Zeus’ counsel sends the divine child to Persephonē (the Zagreus/Dionysos tradition).

line_details.greek: ἀχθε ὶς ἐȟετράφης, φίλος ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν.
line_details.english: being borne, you were reared, dear to the immortal gods.
line_details.note: ἀχθεὶς ἐξετράφης is the likely reading (text shows corruption): “having been borne/carried, you were reared.” φίλος ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν is a standard hymn formula (“dear to the immortal gods”).

text.english: Come propitious, blessed one, and receive these pleasing rites.
text.greek: εὔφρων ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, κεχαρισμένα δ’ ੂερὰ δέȟαι.

line_details.greek: εὔφρων ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, κεχαρισμένα δ’ ੂερὰ δέȟαι.
line_details.english: Come propitious, blessed one, and receive these pleasing rites.
line_details.note: δέχαι is a poetic/variant imperative for “receive” (cf. δέξαι/δέχου). κεχαρισμένα ἱερά = “pleasing/gracious rites,” the offerings of the hymnists.

text.english: I summon Bakchos, pillar‑encircling, bestower of wine, who, coiling all around on every side within the Kadmeian halls, stilled the mighty seethings of the earth, having driven them away; when the fire‑bearing radiance set the whole earth in motion, with the whirrings of the whirlwind; and up sprang the bond of all things.
text.greek: Κικλήσκω Βάκχον περικιόνιον, μεθυδώτην, Καδμείοισι δόμοις ὃς ἑλισσόμενος πέρι πάντη, ἔστησε κρατεροῦς βρασμοὺς γαίης ἀποπέμψας· ἡνίκα πυρφόρος αὐγὴ ἐ κίνησε χθόνα πᾶσαν, πρηστ ῆρος ῥοίζοις · ὃ δ’ ἀνέδραμε δεσμὸς ἁπάντων.

line_details.greek: Κικλήσκω Βάκχον περικιόνιον, μεθυδώτην,
line_details.english: I summon Bakchos, pillar‑encircling, bestower of wine,
line_details.note: perikionion literally “around‑pillared,” an epithet evoking ivy that twines about columns; methydotēs (= μεθυδώτης) is “giver of wine/intoxication.”

line_details.greek: Καδμείοισι δόμοις ὃς ἑλισσόμενος πέρι πάντη,
line_details.english: who, coiling all around on every side within the Kadmeian halls,
line_details.note: “Kadmeian halls” = Thebes (founded by Kadmos). helissomenos (“coiling”) and peri pantē (“all around on every side”) reinforce the imagery of ivy winding about pillars.

line_details.greek: ἔστησε κρατεροῦς βρασμοὺς γαίης ἀποπέμψας·
line_details.english: stilled the mighty seethings of the earth, having driven them away;
line_details.note: brasmoi (“boilings, seethings”) is a vivid metaphor for earthquake‑tremors; estēse … apopempsas = “stilled … by sending [them] away.”

line_details.greek: ἡνίκα πυρφόρος αὐγὴ ἐ κίνησε χθόνα πᾶσαν,
line_details.english: when the fire‑bearing radiance set the whole earth in motion,
line_details.note: pyrphoros augē (“fire‑bearing radiance”) most naturally alludes to the lightning of Zeus; the scene recalls the Theban mythic setting (Semelē’s conflagration) and ensuing earth‑shaking.

line_details.greek: πρηστ ῆρος ῥοίζοις · ὃ δ’ ἀνέδραμε δεσμὸς ἁπάντων.
line_details.english: with the whirrings of the whirlwind; and up sprang the bond of all things.
line_details.note: The transmitted πρηστ ῆρος is to be read πρηστήρος (“of the whirlwind”); ῥοίζοις = “with whirrings/roarings.” “The bond of all things” (desmos hapantōn) likely denotes ivy, which “sprang up” (anédrame, a verb often used of plant growth) and binds/steadies; some read it as a cosmic “bond,” but the ivy imagery fits the context.

text.english: Come, blessed one, Bacchic leader, with rejoicing mind.
text.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, βακχευτά, γεγηθυίαις πραπίδεσσιν.

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, βακχευτά, γεγηθυίαις πραπίδεσσιν.
line_details.english: Come, blessed one, Bacchic leader, with rejoicing mind.
line_details.note: bakcheutā (“Bacchic leader/reveler”) addresses Dionysus as instigator of Bacchic rites. prapides, literally the midriff, denotes the seat of thought/feeling; hence “mind/heart.”

text.english: Hear, father, Sabazios, son of Kronos, illustrious daimon, who Bakchos Dionysos, loud-roaring, the Sewn-in, didst sew into your thigh, so that, perfected, he might come to holy Tmolos, and beside Hippa of the lovely cheeks.
text.greek: Κλῦθι, πάτερ, Κρόνου υἱέ Σαβάζιε, κύδιμε δαῖμον, ὃς Βάκχον Διόνυσον ἐ ρίβρομον, εἰραφιώτην μηρῷ ἐ γκατέραψας, ὅπως τετελεσμένος ἔλθοι Τμῶλον ἐς ἠγάθεον, παρὰ θ’ Ἵ ππαν καλλιπάρῃον.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθι, πάτερ, Κρόνου υἱέ Σαβάζιε, κύδιμε δαῖμον,
line_details.english: Hear, father, Sabazios, son of Kronos, illustrious daimon,
line_details.note: Calling Sabazios “son of Kronos” aligns him with Zeus; daimon here means a divine power, not a malevolent “demon.”

line_details.greek: ὃς Βάκχον Διόνυσον ἐ ρίβρομον, εἰραφιώτην
line_details.english: who Bakchos Dionysos, loud-roaring, the Sewn-in,
line_details.note: eribromos = “loud-roaring”; Eiraphiotēs (“Sewn‑in”) is an epithet of Dionysos referring to his being sewn into Zeus’s thigh. The spacing in the source (ἐ ρίβρομον) reflects a typographical issue; read ἐρίβρομον.

line_details.greek: μηρῷ ἐ γκατέραψας, ὅπως τετελεσμένος ἔλθοι
line_details.english: didst sew into your thigh, so that, perfected, he might come
line_details.note: μηρῷ ἐγκατέραψας is a compound of rhaptō (“stitch”) with preverbs, “sew/fasten in(to)”; it alludes to the myth of Dionysos’s gestation in Zeus’s thigh. τετελεσμένος can mean “brought to completion,” with possible wordplay on teletai (“mysteries”).

line_details.greek: Τμῶλον ἐς ἠγάθεον, παρὰ θ’ Ἵ ππαν καλλιπάρῃον.
line_details.english: to holy Tmolos, and beside Hippa of the lovely cheeks.
line_details.note: Τμῶλος is the Lydian mountain; ἠγάθεον = “holy/sacred.” Ἵππαν (“Hippa”) is likely the Lydian/Phrygian goddess Hipta/Hippa, associated with Sabazios and Dionysos; the identification and form are debated in the tradition.

text.english: But, blessed one, lord of Phrygia, most kingly of all, with good will come as a helper to the mystic celebrants.
text.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, Φρυγίης μεδέων, βασιλεύτατε πάντων, εὐμενέων ἐπαρωγὸς ἐπέλθοις μυστιπόλοισιν.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, Φρυγίης μεδέων, βασιλεύτατε πάντων,
line_details.english: But, blessed one, lord of Phrygia, most kingly of all,

line_details.greek: εὐμενέων ἐπαρωγὸς ἐπέλθοις μυστιπόλοισιν.
line_details.english: with good will come as a helper to the mystic celebrants.
line_details.note: εὐμενέων is a genitive of manner, “with good will.” μυστιπόλοι are “mystery‑servers/celebrants,” those who conduct or participate in the rites; ἐπαρωγός = “helper/ally.”

text.english: I invoke Hipta, nurse of Bakchos, Euiad maiden, mystic-serving, exulting in the rites of holy Sabos, and in the nocturnal choruses of loud‑roaring Iakkhos.
text.greek: Ἵππαν κικλήσκω Βάκχου τροφόν, εὐάδα κούρην, μυστι πόλο ν τελετ ῇσιν ἀγαλλομένην Σάβου ἁγνο ῦ, νυκτερίοισι τε χοροῖσιν ἐριβρεμέταο Ἰάκχου.

line_details.greek: Ἵππαν κικλήσκω Βάκχου τροφόν, εὐάδα κούρην,
line_details.english: I invoke Hipta, nurse of Bakchos, Euiad maiden,
line_details.note: Ἵππαν likely reflects the goddess Hipta (often printed Ἵπτα; acc. Ἵπταν), a Phrygian/Lydian nurse of Dionysus. “Euiad” (εὐάδα) = Bacchic, ‘crying euoi’.

line_details.greek: μυστι πόλο ν τελετ ῇσιν ἀγαλλομένην Σάβου ἁγνο ῦ,
line_details.english: mystic-serving, exulting in the rites of holy Sabos,
line_details.note: μυστιπόλον = ‘minister/attendant of mysteries’; τελεταῖσιν = ‘rites/initiations’. Σάβου (gen.) is probably Sabos = Sabazios, the Anatolian god associated with Dionysiac cult.

line_details.greek: νυκτερίοισι τε χοροῖσιν ἐριβρεμέταο Ἰάκχου.
line_details.english: and in the nocturnal choruses of loud‑roaring Iakkhos.
line_details.note: ἐριβρεμέταο = ‘very‑roaring, thunder‑voiced.’ Ἰάκχος (Iakkhos) is both the cult‑cry and a deity linked with Eleusinian/Dionysiac processions.

text.english: Hear me praying, chthonian Mother, sovereign Queen, whether you hold in Phrygia the holy mount of Ida, or Tmolos delights you, a fair tumult to the Lydians; come to the rites, rejoicing with sacred countenance.
text.greek: κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, χθονίη μήτηρ, βασίλεια, εἴτε σύ γ’ ἐν Φρυγίῃ κατέχεις Ἴδης ὄρος ἁγνὸν, ἢ Τμ ῶλος τέρπει σε, καλὸν Λυδο ῖσι θόασμα· ἔρχεο πρὸς τελετὰς ἱερῷ γηθο ῦσα προσώπῳ.

line_details.greek: κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, χθονίη μήτηρ, βασίλεια,
line_details.english: Hear me praying, chthonian Mother, sovereign Queen,
line_details.note: “Chthonian Mother” may point to Rhea/Kybele or Gaia; the title βασίλεια (‘Queen’) suits an Anatolian Great Mother.

line_details.greek: εἴτε σύ γ’ ἐν Φρυγίῃ κατέχεις Ἴδης ὄρος ἁγνὸν,
line_details.english: whether you hold in Phrygia the holy mount of Ida,
line_details.note: Refers to the Phrygian Ida; the line situates the goddess in Anatolian sacred mountains.

line_details.greek: ἢ Τμ ῶλος τέρπει σε, καλὸν Λυδο ῖσι θόασμα·
line_details.english: or Tmolos delights you, a fair tumult to the Lydians;
line_details.note: θόασμα = ‘rushing noise, din, tumult,’ perhaps of streams (Tmolos/Pactolus) or of orgiastic music; hence ‘fair tumult’ for Lydians.

line_details.greek: ἔρχεο πρὸς τελετὰς ἱερῷ γηθο ῦσα προσώπῳ.
line_details.english: come to the rites, rejoicing with sacred countenance.
line_details.note: ἱερῷ προσώπῳ (‘with holy face’) is a cultic idiom for a gracious epiphany; ἔρχεο is an imperative ‘come’.

text.english: Hear, blessed one, son of Zeus, Iacchos of the wine‑press, twice‑mothered, much‑remembered seed, much‑named, liberating daimon.
text.greek: Κλῦθι, μάκαρ, Διὸς υ ੈ’, ἐπιλήνιε Ǻάκχε, διμήτωρ, σπέρμα πολύμνηστον, πολυώνυμε, λύσιε δαῖμον.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθι, μάκαρ, Διὸς υ ੈ’, ἐπιλήνιε Ǻάκχε, διμήτωρ,
line_details.english: Hear, blessed one, son of Zeus, Iacchos of the wine‑press, twice‑mothered,
line_details.note: ἐπιλήνιε = ‘of/at the wine‑press’ (Lenaean epithet). διμήτωρ = ‘twice‑mothered,’ alluding to Dionysus’ birth from Semelē and from Zeus’ thigh.

line_details.greek: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον, πολυώνυμε, λύσιε δαῖμον.
line_details.english: much‑remembered seed, much‑named, liberating daimon.
line_details.note: σπέρμα πολύμνηστον ‘much‑remembered seed’ evokes the ever‑remembered generative power; λύσιε ‘Liberator’ (Lysios) is a Dionysiac epithet for releasing cares/bonds.

text.english: secretly‑born, holy shoot of the Blessed, Euie Iacchos, well‑nourished, fruitful, fostering the much‑delighting fruit, door‑breaking, Lenaean, mighty in strength, changeful in form; manifest remedy that ends pain for mortals, holy blossom, a joy to mortals, lover of freedom from grief, bringer‑on, fair‑tressed, Liberator, thyrsus‑mad, Bromios, Euie, kindly‑minded to all, upon whom you choose to shine forth among mortals and immortals; now I call you to come sweetly to the mystai, fruit‑bearing.
text.greek: κρυψίγονον μακάρων ੂερὸν θάλος, εὔȧε Ǻάκχε, εὐτραφές, εὔκαρπος, πολυγηθέα καρπὸν ἀέȟων, ῥηȟίχθων, ληναῖε, μεγασθενές, αἰολόμορφε· παυσίπονον θνητοῖσι φανε ὶς ਙκος, ੂερὸν ਙνθος, χάρμα βροτοῖς φιλάλυπον, ἐφάπτορ, καλλιέθειρε, λύσιε, θυρσομανές, βρόμι’, ε ὔȧε, π઼σιν ἐ૥φρων, οੈς ἐθέλεις θνητ૵ν ἠδ’ ἀθανάτων σἐπιφαύσκειν· νῦν σε καλ ૵ μύστૉ σι μολε ῖν ਲδύν, φερέκαρπον.

line_details.greek: κρυψίγονον μακάρων ੂερὸν θάλος, εὔȧε Ǻάκχε,
line_details.english: secretly‑born, holy shoot of the Blessed, Euie Iacchos,
line_details.note: κρυψίγονον ‘secretly born’ (the hidden gestation in Zeus’ thigh). θάλος ‘shoot/sprout’ of vegetation. εὔιε is the Bacchic cry (Euoi). ‘Blessed’ = the gods.

line_details.greek: εὐτραφές, εὔκαρπος , πολυγηθέα καρπὸν ἀέȟων,
line_details.english: well‑nourished, fruitful, fostering the much‑delighting fruit,

line_details.greek: ῥηȟίχθων, ληναῖε, μεγασθενές, αἰολόμορφε·
line_details.english: door‑breaking, Lenaean, mighty in strength, changeful in form;
line_details.note: The transmitted epithet is uncertain; many print ῥηξίθυρε ‘breaker of doors’ (cf. Bacchic assaults in Eur. Bacch.). Hence ‘door‑breaking.’ αἰολόμορφε ‘of changeful form’ marks Dionysus’ polymorphy.

line_details.greek: παυσίπονον θνητοῖσι φανε ὶς ਙκος, ੂερὸν ਙνθος,
line_details.english: manifest remedy that ends pain for mortals, holy blossom,
line_details.note: ἄκος ‘remedy/cure’—wine as a visible, pain‑ending balm; ἄνθος ‘blossom,’ likely of the vine.

line_details.greek: χάρμα βροτοῖς φιλάλυπον, ἐφάπτορ , καλλιέθειρε,
line_details.english: a joy to mortals, lover of freedom from grief, bringer‑on, fair‑tressed,
line_details.note: φιλάλυπον ‘fond of freedom from grief,’ i.e., relieving sorrow. ἐπάκτωρ ‘bringer‑on’ (of desire or Bacchic fervor). καλλιέθειρε ‘fair‑tressed.’

line_details.greek: λύσιε, θυρσομανές, βρόμι’, ε ὔȧε, π઼σιν ἐ૥φρων,
line_details.english: Liberator, thyrsus‑mad, Bromios, Euie, kindly‑minded to all,
line_details.note: θυρσομανές ‘mad for the thyrsus.’ Βρόμιος ‘Roarer.’ Reading ‘πᾶσιν ἐπήφρων’ (‘kindly‑minded to all’); some editors have ἐπήρωος ‘helper to all.’

line_details.greek: οੈς ἐθέλεις θνητ૵ν ἠδ’ ἀθανάτων σἐπιφαύσκειν·
line_details.english: upon whom you choose to shine forth among mortals and immortals;
line_details.note: ἐπιφαύσκειν ‘to shine forth’ is technical for divine epiphany and selective revelation.

line_details.greek: νῦν σε καλ ૵ μύστૉ σι μολε ῖν ਲδύν, φερέκαρπον.
line_details.english: now I call you to come sweetly to the mystai, fruit‑bearing.
line_details.note: μύσται ‘initiates,’ pointing to the Eleusinian Iacchos. φερέκαρπος ‘fruit‑bearing,’ of fertility/viticulture.

text.english: Nymphs, daughters of great‑hearted Oceanos, holding your dwellings beneath the earth’s hollows along watery ways, secret‑stepping, nurses of Bakchos, chthonian, much‑rejoicing, fruit‑fostering, meadow‑maidens, of winding courses, holy, cave‑delighting, rejoicing in grottoes, air‑wandering, of springs, fleet, dew‑clad, light in your footprints, manifest, unseen, vale‑maidens, abounding in flowers, skipping with Pan over the mountains, crying euai, rock‑gushing, clear‑voiced, fountain‑maidens and wood‑ranging, fragrant maidens, white‑clad, fanned by kindly breezes, goatherding, pastoral, dear to wild beasts, splendid‑fruited, thicket‑loving, tender, abundant in nurture, growth‑fostering, maidens Hamadryads, fond of play, of watery ways, Nysian, maddened by the gadfly, healing maidens, delighting in spring, bringing favor to mortals together with Bakchos and Deo, come to the auspicious rites with gladdened heart, pouring a healthful stream in the seasons that foster increase.
text.greek: Νύμφαι, θυγατέρες μεγαλήτορος Ὠκεανοῖο, ὑγροπόροις γαίης ὑπὸ κεύθεσιν οἰκί’ ἔχουσαι, κρυψίδ ομοι, Βάκχοιο τροφοί, χθόνιαι, πολυγηθεῖς, καρποτρόφοι, λειμωνιάδες, σκολιοδρόμοι, ἁγναί, ἀντρο χαρε ῖς, σπήλυγξι κεχαρμέναι, ἠερόφοιτοι. πηγα ῖαι, δρομάδες, δροσοείμονες, ἴχνεσι κοῦφαι · φαινόμεναι, ἀφανεῖς, α ὐλωνιάδες, πολυανθεῖς· σὺν Πανὶ σκιρτ ῶσαι ἀν’ ο ὔρεα, εὐάστειραι, πετρόρυτοι, λιγυραί, κρουνίτιδες ὑλονόμοι τε· παρθένοι εὐώδεις, λευχείμονες, εὔπνοοι αὔραις, αἰπολικαί, νόμιαι, θηρσὶν φίλαι, ἀγλαόκαρποι, δρυμοχαρεῖς, ἁπαλαί, πολυθρέμμονες, αὐξίτροφοί τε· κοῦραι ἁμαδρυάδες, φιλοπαίγμονες, ὑγροκέλευθοι, Νύσιαι, οἰστρομανεῖς, παιωνίδες, εἰαροτερπεῖς, σὺν Βάκχῳ Δηοῖ τε χάριν θνητοῖσι φέρουσαι· ἔλθετ' ἐπ’ εὐφήμοις ἱεροῖς κεχαρηότι θυμῷ, νᾶμα χέουσαι ὑγεινὸν ἀεξιτρόφοισιν ἐν ὥραις.

line_details.greek: Νύμφαι, θυγατέρες μεγαλήτορος Ὠκεανοῖο,
line_details.english: Nymphs, daughters of great‑hearted Oceanos,
line_details.note: μεγαλήτωρ “great‑hearted”; Oceanos is the mythic progenitor of rivers and Nymphs.

line_details.greek: ὑγροπόροις γαίης ὑπὸ κεύθεσιν οἰκί’ ἔχουσαι,
line_details.english: holding your dwellings beneath the earth’s hollows along watery ways,
line_details.note: ὑγροπόροις “with watery passages/ways” evokes subterranean aquifers; ὑπὸ κεύθεσιν “under the hidden hollows.”

line_details.greek: κρυψίδ ομοι, Βάκχοιο τροφοί, χθόνιαι, πολυγηθεῖς,
line_details.english: secret‑stepping, nurses of Bakchos, chthonian, much‑rejoicing,
line_details.note: The epithet is textually uncertain: often κρύφιοι (“hidden”) or κρυψίδρομοι (“secret‑stepping”); I render the sense “secret‑stepping.” “Nurses of Bakchos” reflects Dionysiac nurture myths.

line_details.greek: καρποτρόφοι, λειμωνιάδες, σκολιοδρόμοι, ἁγναί,
line_details.english: fruit‑fostering, meadow‑maidens, of winding courses, holy,
line_details.note: σκολιοδρόμοι “of crooked/winding courses,” suited to meandering stream‑beds; λειμωνιάδες “meadow‑maidens.”

line_details.greek: ἀντρο χαρε ῖς, σπήλυγξι κεχαρμέναι, ἠερόφοιτοι.
line_details.english: cave‑delighting, rejoicing in grottoes, air‑wandering,
line_details.note: ἀντροχαρεῖς “cave‑delighting”; σπήλυγξι “in grottoes”; ἠερόφοιτοι “air‑wandering,” suggesting misty, liminal movement.

line_details.greek: πηγα ῖαι, δρομάδες, δροσοείμονες, ἴχνεσι κοῦφαι ·
line_details.english: of springs, fleet, dew‑clad, light in your footprints,
line_details.note: δροσοείμονες “dew‑clad” (elsewhere a variant δροσοέμβροτοι, “rain‑drenched”); ἴχνεσι κοῦφαι “light in footfall/footprints.”

line_details.greek: φαινόμεναι, ἀφανεῖς, α ὐλωνιάδες, πολυανθεῖς·
line_details.english: manifest, unseen, vale‑maidens, abounding in flowers,
line_details.note: αὐλωνιάδες “Auloniads,” nymphs of dells/vales; the pairing “appearing, unseen” marks their elusive epiphany.

line_details.greek: σὺν Πανὶ σκιρτ ῶσαι ἀν’ ο ὔρεα, εὐάστειραι,
line_details.english: skipping with Pan over the mountains, crying euai,
line_details.note: εὐαστῇραι/εὐάστειραι “crying euai,” the Bacchic shout; σκιρτῶσαι “skipping, frisking.”

line_details.greek: πετρόρυτοι, λιγυραί, κρουνίτιδες ὑλονόμοι τε·
line_details.english: rock‑gushing, clear‑voiced, fountain‑maidens and wood‑ranging,
line_details.note: πετρόρυτοι “gushing from rock”; κρουνίτιδες (also κρήνιτιδες) “fountain‑nymphs”; ὑλονόμοι “wood‑ranging.”

line_details.greek: παρθένοι εὐώδεις, λευχείμονες, εὔπνοοι αὔραις,
line_details.english: fragrant maidens, white‑clad, fanned by kindly breezes,
line_details.note: λευχείμονες “white‑clad”; εὔπνοοι αὔραις “well‑breathed/fanned by kindly breezes” (instrumental dative).

line_details.greek: αἰπολικαί, νόμιαι, θηρσὶν φίλαι, ἀγλαόκαρποι,
line_details.english: goatherding, pastoral, dear to wild beasts, splendid‑fruited,
line_details.note: αἰπολικαί “goatherding”; νόμιαι from νόμιος “pastoral”; θηρσὶν φίλαι “dear to beasts.”

line_details.greek: δρυμοχαρεῖς, ἁπαλαί, πολυθρέμμονες, αὐξίτροφοί τε·
line_details.english: thicket‑loving, tender, abundant in nurture, growth‑fostering,
line_details.note: πολυθρέμμονες “abundant in nurture”; αὐξίτροφοι “growth‑fostering.”

line_details.greek: κοῦραι ἁμαδρυάδες, φιλοπαίγμονες, ὑγροκέλευθοι,
line_details.english: maidens Hamadryads, fond of play, of watery ways,
line_details.note: Ἁμαδρυάδες are tree‑nymphs bound to single trees; ὑγροκέλευθοι “of watery ways/paths.”

line_details.greek: Νύσιαι, οἰστρομανεῖς, παιωνίδες, εἰαροτερπεῖς,
line_details.english: Nysian, maddened by the gadfly, healing maidens, delighting in spring,
line_details.note: Νύσιαι “of Nysa,” the Dionysiac mountain; οἰστρομανεῖς “driven mad by the gadfly” (Bacchic mania); παιωνίδες “healing maidens” (from Paiōn/Paieon).

line_details.greek: σὺν Βάκχῳ Δηοῖ τε χάριν θνητοῖσι φέρουσαι·
line_details.english: bringing favor to mortals together with Bakchos and Deo,
line_details.note: Deo is Demeter; “bringing favor” (χάριν) marks their beneficence with Bakchos and Demeter.

line_details.greek: ἔλθετ' ἐπ’ εὐφήμοις ἱεροῖς κεχαρηότι θυμῷ,
line_details.english: come to the auspicious rites with gladdened heart,
line_details.note: ἐπ’ εὐφήμοις ἱεροῖς “at auspicious/silenced rites,” a ritual formula; κεχαρηότι θυμῷ “with gladdened heart.”

line_details.greek: νᾶμα χέουσαι ὑγεινὸν ἀεξιτρόφοισιν ἐν ὥραις.
line_details.english: pouring a healthful stream in the seasons that foster increase.
line_details.note: νᾶμα “stream, flow”; ἀεξιτρόφοισιν ὥραις “in the seasons that foster increase,” i.e., the growth‑bringing times of year.

text.english: I call upon you, blessed one, of many names, raving-frenzied, Bakcheus, bull-horned, of the wine-press, fire-sowing, Nysios, Releaser, thigh-nurtured, cradle-borne, fire-breathing, and lord of initiations; nocturnal one, Eubouleus, mitra-wearing, thyrsus-shaker; of the ineffable orgia, triple-natured, hidden shoot of Zeus; primordial one, Erikepaios, father and also son of the gods; raw-feaster, scepter-bearer, mad for the choruses, leader of revel-bands; celebrating the holy trieteric festivals amid calms; earth-rending, fire-bright, Epaptor, two-mothered youth, mountain-rover, horned one, fawn-skin-clad, of the biennial rite, Paean, thyrsus-grasping, under-bosomed, cluster-adorned, Bassareus, ivy-delighting, attended by many maidens, and bestower of order, come, blessed one, ever rejoicing, abounding for your initiates.
text.greek: Κικλήσκω σε, μάκαρ, πολυώνυμε, μαινόλα, Βακχεῦ, ταυρόκερως, ληναῖε, πυρίσπορε, Νύσιε, λυσεῦ, μηροτρεφής, λικνῖτα, πυρίπνοε, καὶ τελετάρχα· νυκτέρι’, Εὐβουλεῦ, μιτρηφόρε, θυρσοτινάκτα· ὄργιον ἄῤῥητον, τριφυές, κρύφιον Διὸς ἔρνος · πρωτόγον’, ἠ ρικεπα ῖε, θεῶν πάτερ ἠδὲ καὶ υἱέ· ὠμάδιε, σκηπτοῦχε, χοροιμανές, ἠγέτα κώμων · βακχεύων ἁγίας τριετηρίδας ἀμφὶ γαληνάς · ῥηξίχθων, πυριφεγγές, ἐπάπτορ, κο ῦρε διμήτωρ, οὐρεσιφο ῖτα, κερώς, νεβριδοστόλος, ἀμφιέτηρε, Παι ὰν θυρσεγχής, ὑποκόλπιε, βοτρυόκοσμε, Βάσσαρε, κισσοχαρής, πολυπάρθενε, καὶ διάκοσμε, ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, μύστῃ σι βρύων κεχαρημένος αἰεί.

line_details.greek: Κικλήσκω σε, μάκαρ, πολυώνυμε, μαινόλα, Βακχεῦ,
line_details.english: I call upon you, blessed one, of many names, raving-frenzied, Bakcheus,
line_details.note: poluōnymos highlights Dionysus’ many aspects; mainolas “raving” conveys Bacchic frenzy.

line_details.greek: ταυρόκερως, ληναῖε, πυρίσπορε, Νύσιε, λυσεῦ,
line_details.english: bull-horned, of the wine-press, fire-sowing, Nysios, Releaser,
line_details.note: Nysios refers to Mt. Nysa, his mythical rearing-place; Lēnaios “of the wine-press”; pyrísporos “fire-sowing” evokes torch-lit rites or lightning.

line_details.greek: μηροτρεφής, λικνῖτα, πυρίπνοε, καὶ τελετάρχα·
line_details.english: thigh-nurtured, cradle-borne, fire-breathing, and lord of initiations;
line_details.note: mērotrephēs “thigh-nurtured” (from Zeus’ thigh); liknītās is “of the winnowing-fan,” the infant’s ritual cradle; pyrípnoos “fire-breathing” metaphorically of inspired fervor; teletárchēs “master of initiations.”

line_details.greek: νυκτέρι’, Εὐβουλεῦ, μιτρηφόρε, θυρσοτινάκτα·
line_details.english: nocturnal one, Eubouleus, mitra-wearing, thyrsus-shaker;
line_details.note: Eubouleus is a chthonic epithet/name (“Good Counsellor”); mitrophóros is “mitra-wearing,” an Eastern-style headband; thyrsotinaktas “one who shakes the thyrsus.”

line_details.greek: ὄργιον ἄῤῥητον , τριφυές, κρύφιον Διὸς ἔρνος ·
line_details.english: of the ineffable orgia, triple-natured, hidden shoot of Zeus;
line_details.note: orgíon árrhēton “ineffable rite” evokes mystery secrecy; triphyḗs is “triple-natured” or “thrice-born”; krýphion Dios hérnos “hidden scion of Zeus.”

line_details.greek: πρωτόγον’, ἠ ρικεπα ῖε, θεῶν πάτερ ἠδὲ καὶ υἱέ·
line_details.english: primordial one, Erikepaios, father and also son of the gods;
line_details.note: Prōtógonos and Ērikepaîos are Orphic names of the primordial god applied to Dionysus; “father and also son of the gods” marks his cyclical, generative identity.

line_details.greek: ὠμάδιε, σκηπτοῦχε, χοροιμανές, ἠγέτα κώμων ·
line_details.english: raw-feaster, scepter-bearer, mad for the choruses, leader of revel-bands;
line_details.note: ōmádios “raw-feaster” (sacrificial raw flesh in ecstatic myth/rite); skēptoûkhos “scepter-bearing”; choroimanḗs “mad for the dances”; hēgeta kōmōn “leader of revels.”

line_details.greek: βακχεύων ἁγίας τριετηρίδας ἀμφὶ γαληνάς ·
line_details.english: celebrating the holy trieteric festivals amid calms;
line_details.note: The trieterides are biennial/third-year Dionysiac festivals; galênai “calms” may refer to serene seasons or metaphorical tranquility of the rites.

line_details.greek: ῥηξίχθων, πυριφεγγές, ἐπάπτορ , κο ῦρε διμήτωρ,
line_details.english: earth-rending, fire-bright, Epaptor, two-mothered youth,
line_details.note: rhēxíchthōn “earth-rending”; pyriphenḗs “fire-bright”; Epáptor is uncertain—often “begetter/assailant” (of women), hence a procreative epithet; koûre dimḗtōr “two-mothered youth” (Semele and Zeus’ thigh).

line_details.greek: οὐρεσιφο ῖτα, κερώς, νεβριδοστόλος, ἀμφιέτηρε,
line_details.english: mountain-rover, horned one, fawn-skin-clad, of the biennial rite,
line_details.note: ouresiphōítas “mountain-rover”; kerōs “horned”; nebridóstolos “clad in fawn-skin (nebris)”; amphietēros “of the biennial rite.”

line_details.greek: Παι ὰν θυρσεγχής, ὑποκόλπιε, βοτρυόκοσμε,
line_details.english: Paean, thyrsus-grasping, under-bosomed, cluster-adorned,
line_details.note: Paean is a healer title; thyrsegkhḗs “thyrsus-grasping”; hypokólpios “under-bosomed,” i.e., carried close to the breast/in the garment’s fold; botryókosmos “garlanded with grape-clusters.”

line_details.greek: Βάσσαρε, κισσοχαρής, πολυπάρθενε, καὶ διάκοσμε,
line_details.english: Bassareus, ivy-delighting, attended by many maidens, and bestower of order,
line_details.note: Bassareus (from bassara, a fox- or fawn-skin garment); kissokharḗs “ivy-delighting”; poluparthenos “attended by many maidens” (Maenads); diákosme is uncertain—‘orderer/adorner’ of the world/rites.

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, μύστῃ σι βρύων κεχαρημένος αἰεί.
line_details.english: come, blessed one, ever rejoicing, abounding for your initiates.
line_details.note: bryōn “abounding, teeming”; mystēs “initiate”; kecharēménos “rejoicing/exultant,” fitting the ritual invocation.

text.english: I call Bakkhos Amphietes, chthonian Dionysos, awakened together with the maid Nymphs of lovely tresses; who, abiding beside Persephone’s holy halls, lulls to rest for a three-year span the holy Bacchic rite; and when he himself rouses again the triennial revel, he turns to hymn with his well‑girdled nurses, bedding down and setting dances in motion among the circling Horai.
text.greek: Ἀμφιετῆ καλέω Βάκχον, χθόνιον Διόνυσον, ἐγρόμενον κούραις ἅμα νύμφαις εὐπλοκάμοισιν· ὃς παρὰ Περσεφόνης ἱερο ῖσι δόμοισιν ἰαύων κοιμίζει τριετῆρα χρόνον Βακχήϊον ἁγνόν. αὐτὸς δ’ ἡνίκα τὸν τριετῆ πάλι κῶμον ἐγείρ ῃ, εἰς ὕμνον τρέπεται σὺν ἐϋζώνοισι τιθήναις, εὐνάζων κινῶν τε χορο ὺς ἐνὶ κυκλάσιν ὥραις.

line_details.greek: Ἀμφιετῆ καλέω Βάκχον, χθόνιον Διόνυσον,
line_details.english: I call Bakkhos Amphietes, chthonian Dionysos,
line_details.note: Amphietes is left transliterated; the epithet likely means “wrapped/clad (on all sides),” often taken of Dionysos as richly or ivy‑clad.

line_details.greek: ἐγρόμενον κούραις ἅμα νύμφαις εὐπλοκάμοισιν·
line_details.english: awakened together with the maid Nymphs of lovely tresses;

line_details.greek: ὃς παρὰ Περσεφόνης ἱερο ῖσι δόμοισιν ἰαύων
line_details.english: who, abiding beside Persephone’s holy halls,
line_details.note: ἰαύων = “abiding, sleeping,” underscoring Dionysos’ chthonian aspect beside Persephone.

line_details.greek: κοιμίζει τριετῆρα χρόνον Βακχήϊον ἁγνόν.
line_details.english: lulls to rest for a three-year span the holy Bacchic rite;
line_details.note: Βακχήϊον ἁγνόν is a substantivized neuter, here “the holy Bacchic rite/revel”; the “three‑year span” alludes to the trieteric cycle of Dionysiac festivals.

line_details.greek: αὐτὸς δ’ ἡνίκα τὸν τριετῆ πάλι κῶμον ἐγείρ ῃ,
line_details.english: and when he himself rouses again the triennial revel,
line_details.note: τριετῆ κῶμον = “triennial revel,” i.e., the trieteris of Dionysiac cult.

line_details.greek: εἰς ὕμνον τρέπεται σὺν ἐϋζώνοισι τιθήναις,
line_details.english: he turns to hymn with his well‑girdled nurses,
line_details.note: “Turns to hymn” (εἰς ὕμνον τρέπεται) marks a ritual shift; “well‑girdled nurses” (τιθαῖναι) are the Nymphs who nurtured the god.

line_details.greek: εὐνάζων κινῶν τε χορο ὺς ἐνὶ κυκλάσιν ὥραις.
line_details.english: bedding down and setting dances in motion among the circling Horai.
line_details.note: εὐνάζων is difficult: lit. “bedding/putting to bed”; here taken as “settling/bedding down” before “setting dances in motion.” “Among the circling Horai” may mean amid the cyclical seasons or literally in company with the goddess Horai.

text.english: But come, blessed one, green‑fruited, horn‑bearing, fruitful Bakkhos, step forth to the all‑divine rite with gleaming countenance, brimming with holy, rite‑born fruits.
text.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, χλοόκαρπε, κερασφόρε, κάρπιμε Βάκχε, βα ῖν’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν γανόωντι προσώπῳ, εὐϊέροις καρπο ῖσι τελεσσιγόνοισι βρυάζων.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, χλοόκαρπε, κερασφόρε, κάρπιμε Βάκχε,
line_details.english: But come, blessed one, green‑fruited, horn‑bearing, fruitful Bakkhos,
line_details.note: Epithets: χλοόκαρπε = “green‑fruited/verdant‑fruited”; κερασφόρε = “horn‑bearing” (bull‑horned Dionysos); κάρπιμε = “fruitful.”

line_details.greek: βα ῖν’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν γανόωντι προσώπῳ,
line_details.english: step forth to the all‑divine rite with gleaming countenance,
line_details.note: πάνθειον τελετήν = “all‑divine rite”; γανόωντι προσώπῳ = “with gleaming/brightened face,” suggesting ritual purity.

line_details.greek: εὐϊέροις καρπο ῖσι τελεσσιγόνοισι βρυάζων.
line_details.english: brimming with holy, rite‑born fruits.
line_details.note: τελεσσιγόνοισι = “born of rites/initiations”; βρυάζων = “brimming, swelling,” conveying abundance of sacred fruits.

parts.part_title: Of Seilenos, of the Satyros, of the Bacchoi.

text.english: Hear me, O most-august fosterer, nurse of Bakchos, best by far of the Silenoi, honored by all the gods and by mortal men at the trieteric seasons, pure in rite, venerable, rite-leader of the pastoral thiasos; Eua-shouter, lover of wakefulness, with the well-girdled nurses, leader of the Naiads and the ivy-bearing Bakchai; come hither to the all-divine rite together with all the Satyrs beast-shaped, granting the euas-cry of lord Bakchios, together with the Bakchai, leading forth the holy Lenaiac celebrations that bring the rites to fulfillment, revealing the night-shining orgia in holy initiations, crying euai, thyrsus-loving, bringing calm to the thiasoi.
text.greek: Κλῦθί μευ, ὦ πολύσεμνε τροφεῦ, Βάκχοιο τιθηνέ, Σιλην ῶν ὄχ’ ἄριστε, τετιμένε πᾶσι θεοῖσιν καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἐπὶ τριετηρίσιν ὥραις, ἁγνοτελής, γεραρός, θιάσου νομίου τελετάρχα· εὐαστής, φιλάγρυπνε σὺν εὐζώνοισι τιθήναις, Ναΐσι καὶ Βάκχαις ἡγούμενε κισσοφόροισιν· δεῦρ’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν Σατύροις ἅμα πᾶσιν θηροτύποις, εὔασμα διδοὺς Βακχείου ἄνακτος, σὺν Βάκχαις Λήναια τελεσφόρα σεμνὰ προπέμπων, ὄργια νυκτιφαῆ τελετα ῖς ἁγίαις ἀναφαίνων, εὐάζων, φιλόθυρσε, γαληνιόων θιάσοισιν.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθί μευ, ὦ πολύσεμνε τροφεῦ, Βάκχοιο τιθηνέ,
line_details.english: Hear me, O most-august fosterer, nurse of Bakchos,
line_details.note: ‘Fosterer’ and ‘nurse’ (trophē/ti-thēnē) mark Silenos as Bacchos’ attendant and tutor; Bakchos is transliterated as a divine name.

line_details.greek: Σιλην ῶν ὄχ’ ἄριστε, τετιμένε πᾶσι θεοῖσιν
line_details.english: best by far of the Silenoi, honored by all the gods
line_details.note: Read Σιληνῶν (“of the Silenoi”); Silenoi are Dionysiac companions. τετιμένε is “honored (by),” taking both gods and mortals as agents in the next line.

line_details.greek: καὶ θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν ἐπὶ τριετηρίσιν ὥραις,
line_details.english: and by mortal men at the trieteric seasons,
line_details.note: ‘Trieteric seasons’ (trieterides) are the triennial Dionysiac festivals.

line_details.greek: ἁγνοτελής, γεραρός, θιάσου νομίου τελετάρχα·
line_details.english: pure in rite, venerable, rite-leader of the pastoral thiasos;
line_details.note: ἁγνοτελής = “pure in rites/performing pure rites.” νομίου could mean “pastoral” (from nomē, fitting the rustic thiasos) or “of custom/law” (from nomos); “pastoral” suits the Dionysiac-satyr context. τελετάρχης = “leader of initiations.”

line_details.greek: εὐαστής, φιλάγρυπνε σὺν εὐζώνοισι τιθήναις,
line_details.english: Eua-shouter, lover of wakefulness, with the well-girdled nurses,
line_details.note: εὐαστής = one who cries euai (the Bacchic shout). φιλάγρυπνος = “fond of wakefulness,” i.e., night-vigils. The “well-girdled nurses” are the Nymph-nurses of Dionysus.

line_details.greek: Ναΐσι καὶ Βάκχαις ἡγούμενε κισσοφόροισιν·
line_details.english: leader of the Naiads and the ivy-bearing Bakchai;
line_details.note: Naiads are water nymphs; the Bakchai (“Bacchants”) are the ivy-bearing female devotees of Dionysus.

line_details.greek: δεῦρ’ ἐπὶ πάνθειον τελετὴν Σατύροις ἅμα πᾶσιν
line_details.english: come hither to the all-divine rite together with all the Satyrs
line_details.note: πάνθειος = “all-divine,” marking the rite as of universal divine scope; δεῦρο is a standard epiphanic summons (“come hither”).

line_details.greek: θηροτύποις, εὔασμα διδοὺς Βακχείου ἄνακτος,
line_details.english: beast-shaped, granting the euas-cry of lord Bakchios,
line_details.note: θηροτύποις = “beast-shaped,” a conventional epithet of Satyrs. εὔασμα = the cry euai; here “granting the euas-cry of lord Bakchios.”

line_details.greek: σὺν Βάκχαις Λήναια τελεσφόρα σεμνὰ προπέμπων,
line_details.english: together with the Bakchai, leading forth the holy Lenaiac celebrations that bring the rites to fulfillment,
line_details.note: Λήναια are Dionysiac winter festivals; τελεσφόρα = “bringing rites to fulfillment/consummating.”

line_details.greek: ὄργια νυκτιφαῆ τελετα ῖς ἁγίαις ἀναφαίνων,
line_details.english: revealing the night-shining orgia in holy initiations,
line_details.note: ὄργια are the secret rites of Dionysus (not “orgies” in the modern sense). τελεταί = initiatory rites; νυκτιφαής (“night-shining”) evokes nocturnal revels and torchlight.

line_details.greek: εὐάζων, φιλόθυρσε, γαληνιόων θιάσοισιν.
line_details.english: crying euai, thyrsus-loving, bringing calm to the thiasoi.
line_details.note: φιλόθυρσος = “thyrsus-loving” (the thyrsus is Dionysus’ ivy-twined staff). γαληνιόων = “soothing, bringing calm,” i.e., pacifying the ecstatic bands (thiasoi).

text.english: Ouraniē, much-hymned, smile-loving Aphroditē, sea-born, begetress goddess, lover of all-night rites, august, nocturnal, yoker, weaver of wiles, mother of Constraint, for all things are from you, and you yoke the cosmos beneath your sway; you hold power over the three Moirai, and you beget all things, whatever is in heaven and in the much-fruited earth, and in the depth of the sea; august seatmate of Bakchos, delighting in banquets, arranger of marriage, mother of the Erotes; with Peithō you are bed-delighting, secret one, queen endowed with Graces, both manifest and unseen, lovely-tressed, well-fathered, bridal goddess, feast-companion, scepter-bearing among the gods, she-wolf; giver of birth, man-loving, most longed-for, giver of life; yoking mortals with unbridled compulsions, and the great tribe of beasts, under love-maddening charms,— come, Kyprogenes, of divine lineage, whether on Olympos you abide, queen goddess, rejoicing in your fair face, or you attend the seat of incense-rich Syria, or in the plains, with chariots fashioned of gold, you possess the fertile baths of holy Egypt, or on dark-blue vehicles upon the sea’s swell as you come you delight in the circling dances of the Nereids; or you take pleasure with dark-eyed nymphs on Zeus’s earth, with the Thyads on sandy shores, in a light-leaping bound; or in Kypros, O queen, your nurse—there fair unwed maidens and brides throughout each year sing hymns to you, O blessed one, and holy immortal Adōnis.
text.greek: Οὐρανίη, πολύυμνε, φιλομμειδὴς Ἀφροδίτη, ποντογενής, γενέτειρα θεά, φιλοπάννυχε, σεμνή, νυκτερίη, ζεύκτειρα, δολοπλόκε μῆτερ ἀνάγκης· πάντα γὰρ ἐκ σέθεν ἐστίν, ὑπεζεύξω δέ τε κόσμον· καὶ κρατέεις τρισσῶν μοιρ ῶν, γενν ᾷς δὲ τὰ πάντα, ὅσσα τ’ ἐν οὐρανῳ ἐστι καὶ ἐν γαί ῃ πολυκάρπῳ, ἐν πόντου τε βυθ ῷ· σεμνὴ Βάκχοιο πάρεδρε, τερπομένη θαλί ῃσι, γαμοστόλε, μ ῆτερ ἐρώτων· πειθο ῖ λεκτροχαρής, κρυφίη, χαριδῶτι ἄνασσα, φαινομένη τ’, ἀφανής τ’, ἐ ρατοπλόκαμ’, εὐπατέρεια, νυμφιδίη, σύνδαιτε, θεῶν σκηπτο ῦχε, λύκαινα· γεννοδότειρα, φίλανδρε, ποθεινοτάτη, βιοδ ῶτι· ἐνζεύξασα βροτο ὺς ἀχαλινώτοισιν ἀνάγκαις, καὶ θηρ ῶν πολ ὺ φῦλον, ἐ ρωμανέων ὑπὸ φίλτρων ἔρχεο, Κυπρογενὲς θε ῖον γένος, εἴτ’ ἐν’ Ὀλύμπ ῳ ἐσσί, θεὰ βασίλεια, καλῷ γήθουσα προσώπῳ, εἴτε καὶ εὐλιβάνου Συρίης ἕδος ἀμφιπολεύεις, εἴτε σύ γ’ ἐν πεδίοισι σὺν ἅρμασι χρυσεοτεύκτοις Αἰγύπτου κατέχεις ἱερῆς γονιμώδεα λουτρά, ἢ καὶ κυανέοισιν ὄχοις ἐπὶ πόντιον οἶδμα ἐρχομένη χαίρεις νεπόδων κυκλί ῃσι χορείαις· ἢ νύμφαις τέρπῃ κυανώπισιν ἐν χθον ὶ Δίᾳ, θυι ὰς ἐπ’ αἰγιαλο ῖς ψαμμώδεσιν ἅλματι κούφ ῳ· εἴτ’ ἐν Κύπρῳ, ἄνασσα, τροφ ῷ σέο· ἔνθα καλαί σε παρθένοι ἀδμῆται νύμφαι τ’ ἀνὰ πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸ ν ὑμνο ῦσιν, σέ, μάκαιρα, καὶ ἄμβροτον ἁγνὸν Ἄδωνιν.

line_details.greek: Οὐρανίη , πολύυμνε, φιλομμειδὴς Ἀφροδίτη,
line_details.english: Ouraniē, much-hymned, smile-loving Aphroditē,
line_details.note: Οὐρανίη ‘heavenly/sky-born’; philommeidēs ‘smile-loving’ is a traditional epithet of Aphroditē.

line_details.greek: ποντογενής, γενέτειρα θεά, φιλοπάννυχε, σεμνή,
line_details.english: sea-born, begetress goddess, lover of all-night rites, august,
line_details.note: philopannychos ‘fond of all-night rites/revels’; geneteira ‘begetress’.

line_details.greek: νυκτερίη, ζεύκτειρα, δολοπλόκε μῆτερ ἀνάγκης·
line_details.english: nocturnal, yoker, weaver of wiles, mother of Constraint,
line_details.note: zēukteira ‘yoker, joiner’; doloploke ‘weaver of wiles’; mētēr anankēs may mean ‘mother of Necessity’ (personified Anankē) or ‘source of compulsion’.

line_details.greek: πάντα γὰρ ἐκ σέθεν ἐστίν, ὑπεζεύξω δέ τε κόσμον·
line_details.english: for all things are from you, and you yoke the cosmos beneath your sway;
line_details.note: hypezēuxō is formally aorist 2nd sg., often understood with gnomic/present force: ‘you yoke’ (bring under your yoke) the kosmos.

line_details.greek: καὶ κρατέεις τρισσῶν μοιρ ῶν, γενν ᾷς δὲ τὰ πάντα,
line_details.english: you hold power over the three Moirai, and you beget all things,
line_details.note: Moirai = the three Fates; gennāis ‘you beget’ stresses cosmic generativity.

line_details.greek: ὅσσα τ’ ἐν οὐρανῳ ἐστι καὶ ἐν γαί ῃ πολυκάρπῳ,
line_details.english: whatever is in heaven and in the much-fruited earth,
line_details.note: polykárpos ‘much-fruited/abundant in fruit’.

line_details.greek: ἐν πόντου τε βυθ ῷ· σεμνὴ Βάκχοιο πάρεδρε,
line_details.english: and in the depth of the sea; august seatmate of Bakchos,
line_details.note: páredros ‘seatmate/attendant’; here ‘consort/partner’ of Bakchos (Dionysos), reflecting Orphic syncretism.

line_details.greek: τερπομένη θαλί ῃσι, γαμοστόλε, μ ῆτερ ἐρώτων·
line_details.english: delighting in banquets, arranger of marriage, mother of the Erotes;
line_details.note: thalíai ‘banquets/festive feasts’; gamostolé ‘marriage-arranger’; Erotes = winged Loves.

line_details.greek: πειθο ῖ λεκτροχαρής, κρυφίη, χαριδῶτι ἄνασσα,
line_details.english: with Peithō you are bed-delighting, secret one, queen endowed with Graces,
line_details.note: Peithō personified Persuasion; lektra-charēs ‘bed-delighting’; charidōti ‘grace-endowed’ evokes the Charites (Graces).

line_details.greek: φαινομένη τ’, ἀφανής τ’, ἐ ρατοπλόκαμ’, εὐπατέρεια,
line_details.english: both manifest and unseen, lovely-tressed, well-fathered,
line_details.note: ‘Manifest and unseen’ balances epiphany and hidden presence; eratoplokamos ‘lovely-locked’; eupatereia ‘well-sired’ (father variously given as Ouranos/Zeus in different traditions).

line_details.greek: νυμφιδίη, σύνδαιτε, θεῶν σκηπτο ῦχε, λύκαινα·
line_details.english: bridal goddess, feast-companion, scepter-bearing among the gods, she-wolf;
line_details.note: nymphidíē ‘of brides/bridal’; syndáite ‘feast-companion’; theōn skēptouchos ‘scepter-holder among the gods’; lykaina ‘she-wolf’ may hint at fierce/rapacious desire or protective fierceness.

line_details.greek: γεννοδότειρα, φίλανδρε, ποθεινοτάτη, βιοδ ῶτι·
line_details.english: giver of birth, man-loving, most longed-for, giver of life;
line_details.note: gennodoteira ‘giver of birth’; potheinotatē superlative ‘most longed-for’; biodōti ‘giver of life/livelihood’.

line_details.greek: ἐνζεύξασα βροτο ὺς ἀχαλινώτοισιν ἀνάγκαις,
line_details.english: yoking mortals with unbridled compulsions,
line_details.note: enzéuxasa ‘having yoked’; achalinōtois anankais ‘unbridled compulsions’ (oxymoronic, expressing irresistible erotic constraint).

line_details.greek: καὶ θηρ ῶν πολ ὺ φῦλον, ἐ ρωμανέων ὑπὸ φίλτρων
line_details.english: and the great tribe of beasts, under love-maddening charms,—
line_details.note: erōmaneōn philtrōn ‘love-maddening charms/philters’; philtra are magical love-charms.

line_details.greek: ἔρχεο, Κυπρογενὲς θε ῖον γένος, εἴτ’ ἐν’ Ὀλύμπ ῳ
line_details.english: come, Kyprogenes, of divine lineage, whether on Olympos
line_details.note: Kyprogenes ‘born of/at Cyprus’; theion genos ‘of divine stock/kind’.

line_details.greek: ἐσσί, θεὰ βασίλεια, καλῷ γήθουσα προσώπῳ,
line_details.english: you abide, queen goddess, rejoicing in your fair face,
line_details.note: No special difficulty; the verse highlights epiphanic beauty (‘fair face’).

line_details.greek: εἴτε καὶ εὐλιβάνου Συρίης ἕδος ἀμφιπολεύεις,
line_details.english: or you attend the seat of incense-rich Syria,
line_details.note: eulibanos ‘rich in incense’: Syria evokes Near Eastern cults (Astarte/Ishtar affinities).

line_details.greek: εἴτε σύ γ’ ἐν πεδίοισι σὺν ἅρμασι χρυσεοτεύκτοις
line_details.english: or in the plains, with chariots fashioned of gold,
line_details.note: chryseo-teuktos ‘golden-wrought’; pedía ‘plains’.

line_details.greek: Αἰγύπτου κατέχεις ἱερῆς γονιμώδεα λουτρά,
line_details.english: you possess the fertile baths of holy Egypt,
line_details.note: gonimōdea loútra ‘fertile baths’: likely alluding to the Nile’s life-giving waters/ritual pools; katecheis ‘you possess/hold’.

line_details.greek: ἢ καὶ κυανέοισιν ὄχοις ἐπὶ πόντιον οἶδμα
line_details.english: or on dark-blue vehicles upon the sea’s swell
line_details.note: ochos ‘vehicle/chariot’; kyaneos ‘dark-blue’ fits marine imagery.

line_details.greek: ἐρχομένη χαίρεις νεπόδων κυκλί ῃσι χορείαις·
line_details.english: as you come you delight in the circling dances of the Nereids;
line_details.note: nepodōn is textually uncertain; commonly taken as ‘of the Nereids’ (sea-nymphs), and translated accordingly.

line_details.greek: ἢ νύμφαις τέρπῃ κυανώπισιν ἐν χθον ὶ Δίᾳ,
line_details.english: or you take pleasure with dark-eyed nymphs on Zeus’s earth,
line_details.note: chthoni Diā: either ‘on Zeus’s earth’ (the inhabited world) or the island Dia (near Crete); ambiguity likely intentional.

line_details.greek: θυι ὰς ἐπ’ αἰγιαλο ῖς ψαμμώδεσιν ἅλματι κούφ ῳ·
line_details.english: with the Thyads on sandy shores, in a light-leaping bound;
line_details.note: Thyíai/Thyads = Bacchic women; image of ecstatic leaping on the shore links Dionysian and Aphrodisian rites.

line_details.greek: εἴτ’ ἐν Κύπρῳ, ἄνασσα, τροφ ῷ σέο· ἔνθα καλαί σε
line_details.english: or in Kypros, O queen, your nurse—there
line_details.note: trophos ‘nurse’: Cyprus as Aphroditē’s nurturer.

line_details.greek: παρθένοι ἀδμῆται νύμφαι τ’ ἀνὰ πάντ’ ἐνιαυτὸ ν
line_details.english: fair unwed maidens and brides throughout each year
line_details.note: admētai ‘unwed/untamed’ maidens; yearly hymning indicates ongoing cult.

line_details.greek: ὑμνο ῦσιν, σέ, μάκαιρα, καὶ ἄμβροτον ἁγνὸν Ἄδωνιν.
line_details.english: sing hymns to you, O blessed one, and holy immortal Adōnis.
line_details.note: Calling Adōnis ‘ambrotos, hagnos’ (immortal, holy) is cultic hyperbole, despite his mythic mortality.

text.english: Come, blessed goddess, bearing a most lovely form, for with a solemn soul I summon you with holy words.
text.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρα θεά, μάλ’ ἐπήρατον εἶδος ἔχουσα ψυχ ῇ γάρ σε καλῶ σεμν ῇ ἁγίοισι λόγοισιν.

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαιρα θεά, μάλ’ ἐπήρατον εἶδος ἔχουσα
line_details.english: Come, blessed goddess, bearing a most lovely form,
line_details.note: No special difficulty.

line_details.greek: ψυχ ῇ γάρ σε καλῶ σεμν ῇ
line_details.english: for with a solemn soul I summon you
line_details.note: Standard Orphic closure: with a ‘reverent/august’ soul (semnē psychē).

line_details.greek: ἁγίοισι λόγοισιν.
line_details.english: with holy words.
line_details.note: Formulaic ending invoking ‘holy words’ (hagioi logoi).

text.english: Hear me as I pray, O much‑named one, noblest daimon, soft‑tressed, lover of lonely places, teeming with the longed‑for seasons, Eubouleus, many‑shaped, manifest nourisher of all.
text.greek: Κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, πολυώνυμε, δαῖμον ἄριστε, ἁβροκόμη, φιλέρημε, βρύων ὥρῃσι ποθεινα ῖς, Εὐβουλεῦ, πολύμορφε, τροφεῦ πάντων ἀρίδηλε.

line_details.greek: Κλῦθί μευ εὐχομένου, πολυώνυμε, δαῖμον ἄριστε,
line_details.english: Hear me as I pray, O much‑named one, noblest daimon,
line_details.note: “daimon” preserves the Greek term for a divine spirit; polyonymos = “much‑named.”

line_details.greek: ἁβροκόμη, φιλέρημε, βρύων ὥρῃσι ποθεινα ῖς,
line_details.english: soft‑tressed, lover of lonely places, teeming with the longed‑for seasons,
line_details.note: φιλέρημε (‘philērēme’) literally “fond of lonely/solitary places” (from ἐρῆμος); βρύων “teeming, swelling,” here of seasonal growth.

line_details.greek: Εὐβουλεῦ, πολύμορφε, τροφεῦ πάντων ἀρίδηλε.
line_details.english: Eubouleus, many‑shaped, manifest nourisher of all.
line_details.note: Eubouleus is a chthonic epithet (often of Hades/Dionysus), signaling syncretism; πολύμορφος = “many‑shaped”; ἀρίδηλος = “manifest, plain to see.”

text.english: boy and maiden; an ever‑fair blossom for all, Adonis, quenched yet radiant within the fair cycles of the Horai; luxuriantly‑growing, two‑horned, much‑desired, honored with tears, bright in form, rejoicing in the hunt, long‑haired; yearning‑souled, sweet blossom of Kypris, shoot of Eros; born in the beds of lovely‑tressed Persephone; you who at one time dwell beneath misty Tartaros, and again you bring your season‑ripe form back toward Olympos; come, blessed one, bringing from the earth fruits for the initiates.
text.greek: κούρη καὶ κόρε· πᾶσι καλ ὸν θάλος αἰὲν, Ἄ δωνι, σβεννύμενος λάμπων τε καλαῖς ἐν κυκλάσιν ὥραις· αὐξιθαλής, δίκερως, πολυήρατε, δακρυότιμε, ἀγλαόμορφε, κυνηγεσίαις χαίρων, βαθυχα ῖτα· ἱμερόνους, Κύπριδος γλυκερὸν θάλος, ἔρνο ς ἔρωτος· Φερσεφόνης ἐρασιπλοκάμου λέκτροισι λοχευθείς · ὃς ποτ ὲ μὲν ναίεις ὑπὸ Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα, ἠδὲ πάλιν πρ ὸς Ὄλυμπον ἄγεις δέμας ὡριόκαρπον ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, μύστῃ σι φέρων καρποὺς ἀπὸ γαίης.

line_details.greek: κούρη καὶ κόρε· πᾶσι καλ ὸν θάλος αἰὲν, Ἄ δωνι,
line_details.english: boy and maiden; an ever‑fair blossom for all, Adonis,
line_details.note: κούρη καὶ κόρε (“boy and maiden”) marks an androgynous or bi‑gendered aspect; θάλος “blossom” is a set metaphor for youthful beauty. Vocative Ἄδωνι is standard in cult address.

line_details.greek: σβεννύμενος λάμπων τε καλαῖς ἐν κυκλάσιν ὥραις·
line_details.english: quenched yet radiant within the fair cycles of the Horai;
line_details.note: σβεννύμενος/λάμπων (“quenched yet shining”) is a deliberate paradox of extinction and return; Ὧραι (Horai) are the Seasons personified; κυκλάσιν “cycles.”

line_details.greek: αὐξιθαλής, δίκερως, πολυήρατε, δακρυότιμε,
line_details.english: luxuriantly‑growing, two‑horned, much‑desired, honored with tears,
line_details.note: δίκερως “two‑horned” (perhaps lunar/bovine or venatic); δακρυότιμος “honored with tears,” alluding to Adonis‑laments.

line_details.greek: ἀγλαόμορφε, κυνηγεσίαις χαίρων, βαθυχα ῖτα·
line_details.english: bright in form, rejoicing in the hunt, long‑haired;
line_details.note: βαθυχαίτας “deep‑haired” = long‑haired; κυνηγεσίαις χαίρων “rejoicing in the hunt.”

line_details.greek: ἱμερόνους, Κύπριδος γλυκερὸν θάλος, ἔρνο ς ἔρωτος·
line_details.english: yearning‑souled, sweet blossom of Kypris, shoot of Eros;
line_details.note: ἱμερόνους “yearning‑souled, desire‑minded”; Kypris = Aphrodite; ἔρνος ἔρωτος “shoot/sprout of Eros.”

line_details.greek: Φερσεφόνης ἐρασιπλοκάμου λέκτροισι λοχευθείς ·
line_details.english: born in the beds of lovely‑tressed Persephone;
line_details.note: λοχευθείς (from λοχεύω “to bring to birth”): “born in the beds of Persephone,” reflecting an Orphic/chthonic variant of the Adonis myth.

line_details.greek: ὃς ποτ ὲ μὲν ναίεις ὑπὸ Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα,
line_details.english: you who at one time dwell beneath misty Tartaros,
line_details.note: ἀηερόεντα/ἠερόεντα = “misty, murky”; Tartaros is the underworld abyss.

line_details.greek: ἠδὲ πάλιν πρ ὸς Ὄλυμπον ἄγεις δέμας ὡριόκαρπον
line_details.english: and again you bring your season‑ripe form back toward Olympos;
line_details.note: ὡριόκαρπον “season‑ripe”; δέμας “form, body.” The line describes cyclical descent and return.

line_details.greek: ἐλθέ, μάκαρ, μύστῃ σι φέρων καρποὺς ἀπὸ γαίης.
line_details.english: come, blessed one, bringing from the earth fruits for the initiates.
line_details.note: μύστῃσι dat. pl. “for the initiates (mystai)”; the fruits are both literal and symbolic of fertility/prosperity.

text.english: Dwelling by Kokytos, the unreturning road of Ananke, you who lead the souls of mortals down beneath the nether earth, Hermes, offspring of Bacchic-dancing Dionysos, and of the Paphian maiden, curl-lashed Aphrodite, you who attend about Persephone’s sacred house, being the escort for the grim-fated souls beneath the earth; whom you bring down whenever the time of fate has arrived, charming all with your well-hallowed, sleep-bestowing staff, and again you rouse those who slumber; for to you the goddess Persephone granted honor, down through broad Tartaros, to lead the way for the ever-flowing souls of mortals.
text.greek: Κωκυτο ῦ ναίων ἀνυπόστροφον οἶμον ἀνάγκης, ὃς ψυχ ὰς θνητῶν κατάγεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα γαίης, Ἑρμῆ, βακχεχόροιο Διωνύσοιο γένεθλον, καὶ Παφίης κούρης, ἑλικοβλεφάρου Ἀφροδίτης, ὃς παρὰ Περσεφόνης ἱερὸν δόμον ἀμφιπολεύεις, αἰνομόροις ψυχαῖς πομπὸς κατὰ γαῖαν ὑπάρχων· ἃς κατάγεις, ὁπόταν μοίρης χρόνος εἰσαφίκηται, εὐϊέρῳ ῥάβδῳ θέλγων ὑπνοδώτιδι πάντα, καὶ πάλιν ὑπνώοντας ἐγείρεις. σοὶ γὰρ ἔδωκεν τιμ ὴν Φερσεφόνεια θεὰ, κατὰ Τάρταρο ν εὐρὺν ψυχαῖς ἀενάοις θνητῶν ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύειν.

line_details.greek: Κωκυτο ῦ ναίων ἀνυπόστροφον οἶμον ἀνάγκης,
line_details.english: Dwelling by Kokytos, the unreturning road of Ananke,
line_details.note: Κωκυτοῦ ‘of Kokytos’ (the river of lamentation); ἀνυπόστροφον ‘of no turning back’; οἶμον ἀνάγκης ‘the road of Necessity (Ananke)’. The participle ναίων ‘dwelling’ governs the genitive.

line_details.greek: ὃς ψυχ ὰς θνητῶν κατάγεις ὑπὸ νέρτερα γαίης,
line_details.english: you who lead the souls of mortals down beneath the nether earth,
line_details.note: νέρτερα γαίης ‘the nether regions of the earth’ is a conventional periphrasis for the underworld.

line_details.greek: Ἑρμῆ , βακχεχόροιο Διωνύσοιο γένεθλον,
line_details.english: Hermes, offspring of Bacchic-dancing Dionysos,
line_details.note: βακχεχόροιο ‘of Bacchic dance’; γένεθλον ‘offspring/descent’. Calling Hermes the child of Dionysos (and Aphrodite in the next line) is an Orphic variant that has troubled editors; some suspect contamination with hymns to Priapos or Hermaphroditos.

line_details.greek: καὶ Παφίης κούρης, ἑλικοβλεφάρου Ἀφροδίτης,
line_details.english: and of the Paphian maiden, curl-lashed Aphrodite,
line_details.note: Παφίης κούρης ‘the Paphian maiden’ = Aphrodite; ἑλικοβλεφάρου ‘with curling lashes’ is a Homeric-style epithet of feminine beauty.

line_details.greek: ὃς παρὰ Περσεφόνης ἱερὸν δόμον ἀμφιπολεύεις,
line_details.english: you who attend about Persephone’s sacred house,
line_details.note: ἀμφιπολεύεις ‘you attend/minister about’ emphasizes Hermes’ chthonic service at Persephone’s house.

line_details.greek: αἰνομόροις ψυχαῖς πομπὸς κατὰ γαῖαν ὑπάρχων·
line_details.english: being the escort for the grim-fated souls beneath the earth;
line_details.note: αἰνομόροις ‘grim‑fated’; πομπός ‘escort’ evokes Hermes’ title Psychopompos. κατὰ γαῖαν here means ‘beneath/through the earth’.

line_details.greek: ἃς κατάγεις, ὁπόταν μοίρης χρόνος εἰσαφίκηται,
line_details.english: whom you bring down whenever the time of fate has arrived,
line_details.note: μοίρης χρόνος ‘the appointed time of fate’; εἰσαφίκηται ‘has arrived’ is an epic compound.

line_details.greek: εὐϊέρῳ ῥάβδῳ θέλγων ὑπνοδώτιδι πάντα,
line_details.english: charming all with your well-hallowed, sleep-bestowing staff,
line_details.note: εὐϊέρῳ ‘well-hallowed’; ὑπνοδώτιδι ‘sleep-giving’ modifies ῥάβδῳ ‘staff’. The sleep-charming wand recalls Homeric Hermes (Od. 5.47–54).

line_details.greek: καὶ πάλιν ὑπνώοντας ἐγείρεις. σοὶ γὰρ ἔδωκεν
line_details.english: and again you rouse those who slumber; for to you
line_details.note: No special difficulty; the line completes the thought of 8 and leads to the divine grant in 10.

line_details.greek: τιμ ὴν Φερσεφόνεια θεὰ, κατὰ Τάρταρο ν εὐρὺν
line_details.english: the goddess Persephone granted honor, down through broad Tartaros,
line_details.note: Φερσεφόνεια is a variant form of Persephone; κατὰ Τάρταρον εὐρύν ‘down through broad Tartaros’, with κατά expressing extension into depth.

line_details.greek: ψυχαῖς ἀενάοις θνητῶν ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύειν.
line_details.english: to lead the way for the ever-flowing souls of mortals.
line_details.note: ἀενάοις ‘ever-flowing/perpetual’ of the stream of souls; ἡγεμονεύειν ‘to lead/guide’ reiterates Hermes’ psychopompic role.

text.english: But, blessed one, send the mystai a good end upon their deeds.
text.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πέμποις μύσταις τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἔπ’ ἔργοις.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, πέμποις μύσταις τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἔπ’ ἔργοις.
line_details.english: But, blessed one, send the mystai a good end upon their deeds.
line_details.note: μύσταις ‘mystai, initiates’ retained in transliteration; τέλος ἐσθλόν ‘a good end/outcome’ carries eschatological force in Orphic prayer.

text.english: I call upon great, pure, beloved, sweet Eros, bow-armed, winged, fire-running, swift in onset, playing with the gods and with mortal human beings; deft-handed, two-natured, holding the keys of all, of the heavenly aether, the sea, the earth, and whatever to mortals all-begotten breathing creatures the grass-fruited goddess nourishes, and all that wide Tartaros holds, and the loud-roaring sea; for of all these you alone indeed wield the sway.
text.greek: Κικλήσκω μέγαν ἁγνό ν ἐράσμιον ἡδὺν Ἔρωτα, τοξαλκ ῆ, πτερόεντα, πυρίδρομον, εὔδρομον ὁρμῇ, συμπαίζοντα θεοῖς ἠδὲ θνητο ῖς ἀνθρώποις· εὐπάλαμον, διφυῆ, πάντων κλη ῗδας ἔχοντα, αἰθέρος οὐρανίου, πόντου, χθονός, ἠδ’ ὅσα θνητο ῖς πνεύματα παντογένεθλα θεὰ βόσκει χλοόκαρπος, ἠδ’ ὅσα Τ άρταρος εὐρὺς ἔχει, πόντος θ’ ἁλίδουπος · μοῦνος γὰρ τούτων πάντων οἴηκα κρατύνεις.

line_details.greek: Κικλήσκω μέγαν ἁγνό ν ἐράσμιον ἡδὺν Ἔρωτα,
line_details.english: I call upon great, pure, beloved, sweet Eros,

line_details.greek: τοξαλκ ῆ, πτερόεντα, πυρίδρομον, εὔδρομον ὁρμῇ,
line_details.english: bow-armed, winged, fire-running, swift in onset,
line_details.note: Epithets: toxalkēs = ‘bow-armed’; pyridromos = ‘fire-running’ (i.e., moving with the speed of fire); eúdromos hormē = ‘swift in onset/impulse.’

line_details.greek: συμπαίζοντα θεοῖς ἠδὲ θνητο ῖς ἀνθρώποις·
line_details.english: playing with the gods and with mortal human beings;
line_details.note: ‘Playing’ (sympaizonta) conveys Eros’ sportive yet pervasive activity among gods and humans.

line_details.greek: εὐπάλαμον, διφυῆ, πάντων κλη ῗδας ἔχοντα,
line_details.english: deft-handed, two-natured, holding the keys of all,
line_details.note: eupálamos = ‘good in the hand,’ hence ‘deft-handed’; difyēs = ‘two-natured,’ often of Orphic Eros as androgynous or embodying cosmic dualities; ‘keys’ signify cosmic governance of realms.

line_details.greek: αἰθέρος οὐρανίου, πόντου, χθονός, ἠδ’ ὅσα θνητο ῖς
line_details.english: of the heavenly aether, the sea, the earth, and whatever to mortals

line_details.greek: πνεύματα παντογένεθλα θεὰ βόσκει χλοόκαρπος,
line_details.english: all-begotten breathing creatures the grass-fruited goddess nourishes,
line_details.note: pneumata pantogenethla literally ‘all-begotten breaths/spirits,’ here ‘breathing creatures’; thea chloókarpos ‘grass-fruited goddess’ is commonly Gaia or Demeter as nourisher.

line_details.greek: ἠδ’ ὅσα Τ άρταρος εὐρὺς ἔχει, πόντος θ’ ἁλίδουπος ·
line_details.english: and all that wide Tartaros holds, and the loud-roaring sea;

line_details.greek: μοῦνος γὰρ τούτων πάντων οἴηκα κρατύνεις.
line_details.english: for of all these you alone indeed wield the sway.
line_details.note: The transmitted οἴηκα is best taken as οἴη κα(ί) ‘alone indeed’; hence the emphatic ‘you alone indeed’ rule all these. Kratyneis = ‘wield mastery, exercise dominion.’

text.english: But, blessed one, with pure intentions come to the initiates, and drive away from them base and alien impulses.
text.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, καθαραῖς γνώμαις μύστῃ σι συνέρχου, φαύλους δ’ ἐκτοπίους θ’ ὁρμὰ ς ἀπὸ τῶνδ’ ἀπόπεμπε.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά, μάκαρ, καθαραῖς γνώμαις μύστῃ σι συνέρχου,
line_details.english: But, blessed one, with pure intentions come to the initiates,
line_details.note: mystēsi = ‘to the initiates’ (mystai); synerchou = ‘come/attend, join with’ in a ritual sense; gnōmais = ‘intentions, thoughts.’

line_details.greek: φαύλους δ’ ἐκτοπίους θ’ ὁρμὰ ς ἀπὸ τῶνδ’ ἀπόπεμπε.
line_details.english: and drive away from them base and alien impulses.
line_details.note: phaulous … ektopious hormas = ‘base and out-of-place (alien) impulses,’ a standard Orphic prayer for moral purification of initiates.

text.english: Boundless Moirai, dear children of black Nyx, hear me praying, you many-named, who by the lake of heaven (where the white water of night, by nocturnal heat, bursts forth in the shady recess of a sleek-stoned, well-rocked cave), dwelling there, yet you flit over the boundless earth of mortals, whence toward the mortal, slavish race, with light hope, you go, veiling yourselves in purple linens, in the fated plain, where Glory drives the all-embracing chariot beside the boundary of Justice and of Hope and of cares, and the Ogygian ordinance, the origin of boundlessly well-ordered rule.
text.greek: Μοῖραι ἀπειρέσιοι, Νυκτὸς φίλα τέκνα μελαίνης, κλῦτέ μου εὐχομένου, πολυώνυμοι, αἵτ’ ἐπὶ λίμνης οὐρανίας, (ἵνα λευκ ὸν ὕδωρ νυχίας ὑπὸ θερμ ῆς ῥήγνυται ἐν σκιερ ῷ λιπαρο ῦ μυχ ῷ εὐλίθου ἄντρου) ναίουσαι, πεπότησθε βροτῶν ἐπ’ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν ἔνθεν ἐπὶ βρότεον δοῦλον γένος ἐλπίδι κοῦφῃ στείχετε πορφυρέ ῃσι καλ υψάμεναι ὀθόν ῃσι, μορσίμῷ ἐν πεδί ῳ, ὅ θι πάγγεον ἅρμα διώκει δόξα, δίκης παρὰ τέρμα καὶ ἐλπίδος ἠδὲ μεριμν ῶν, καὶ νόμου ὠγύγιον παναπείρονος εὐνόμου ἀρχῆς.

line_details.greek: Μοῖραι ἀπειρέσιοι, Νυκτὸς φίλα τέκνα μελαίνης,
line_details.english: Boundless Moirai, dear children of black Nyx,
line_details.note: ἀπειρέσιοι = “boundless,” a Homeric-form epithet; Nyx is the personified Night.

line_details.greek: κλῦτέ μου εὐχομένου, πολυώνυμοι, αἵτ’ ἐπὶ λίμνης
line_details.english: hear me praying, you many-named, who by the lake
line_details.note: πολυώνυμοι (“many-named”) is a cultic epithet signaling multiple epithets/titles of the goddesses.

line_details.greek: οὐρανίας, (ἵνα λευκ ὸν ὕδωρ νυχίας ὑπὸ θερμ ῆς
line_details.english: of heaven (where the white water of night, by nocturnal heat,
line_details.note: The imagery of the “heavenly lake” and “white water of night” is obscure; many take it as an allusion to the Milky Way. νυχίας ὑπὸ θερμῆς (“by nocturnal heat”) is puzzling and may conceal textual difficulties.

line_details.greek: ῥήγνυται ἐν σκιερ ῷ λιπαρο ῦ μυχ ῷ εὐλίθου ἄντρου)
line_details.english: bursts forth in the shady recess of a sleek-stoned, well-rocked cave),
line_details.note: λιπαρός literally “sleek, shining,” here of the cave; εὐλίθου “well-stoned” (i.e., smoothly rock-lined).

line_details.greek: ναίουσαι, πεπότησθε βροτῶν ἐπ’ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν
line_details.english: dwelling there, yet you flit over the boundless earth of mortals,
line_details.note: πεπότησθε is formally a perfect but often carries present sense (“you fly/flit”) in epic diction.

line_details.greek: ἔνθεν ἐπὶ βρότεον δοῦλον γένος ἐλπίδι κοῦφῃ
line_details.english: whence toward the mortal, slavish race, with light hope,
line_details.note: δοῦλον γένος (“slavish race”) is a traditional Orphic-Anthropogonic topos; ἐλπίδι κοῦφῃ = “with light/fickle hope.”

line_details.greek: στείχετε πορφυρέ ῃσι καλ υψάμεναι ὀθόν ῃσι,
line_details.english: you go, veiling yourselves in purple linens,
line_details.note: ὀθόναι are fine linen veils; πορφυρέαι denotes purple (royal/ritual) coloration.

line_details.greek: μορσίμῷ ἐν πεδί ῳ, ὅ θι πάγγεον ἅρμα διώκει
line_details.english: in the fated plain, where Glory drives the all-embracing chariot
line_details.note: δόξα (nominative) is the subject of διώκει; πάγγεον ἅρμα (“all-embracing chariot”) is uncertain in force—likely a cosmic vehicle of governance.

line_details.greek: δόξα, δίκης παρὰ τέρμα καὶ ἐλπίδος ἠδὲ μεριμν ῶν,
line_details.english: beside the boundary of Justice and of Hope and of cares,
line_details.note: παρὰ τέρμα = “beside the boundary/limit,” marking a liminal cosmic region in which abstract powers are localized.

line_details.greek: καὶ νόμου ὠγύγιον παναπείρονος εὐνόμου ἀρχῆς.
line_details.english: and the Ogygian ordinance, the origin of boundlessly well-ordered rule.
line_details.note: ὠγύγιον = “Ogygian, primeval”; ἀρχή “origin/principle”; the phrase presents primordial Law as source of boundless, well-ordered rule.

text.english: For in life only Moira sees clearly, and no other of the immortals who hold the peak of snowy Olympos, nor even the perfect eye of Zeus; since whatever befalls us, Moira and the mind of Zeus know all things through and through.
text.greek: Μοῖρα γὰρ ἐν βιότ ῳ καθορ ᾷ μόνον, οὐδέ τις ἄλλος ἀθανάτων, οἳ ἔχουσι κάρη νιφόεντος Ὀλύμπου, καὶ Διὸς ὄμμα τέλειον ἐπεί γ’ ὅσα γίγνεται ἡμῖν, Μοῖρά τε καὶ Διὸς ο ἶδε νόος δι ὰπαντὸς ἅπαντα.

line_details.greek: Μοῖρα γὰρ ἐν βιότ ῳ καθορ ᾷ μόνον , οὐδέ τις ἄλλος
line_details.english: For in life only Moira sees clearly, and no other
line_details.note: Μοῖρα in the singular personifies Fate; the exclusivity (“only Moira sees”) sets up the contrast with Zeus in the next lines.

line_details.greek: ἀθανάτων, οἳ ἔχουσι κάρη νιφόεντος Ὀλύμπου,
line_details.english: of the immortals who hold the peak of snowy Olympos,

line_details.greek: καὶ Διὸς ὄμμα τέλειον ἐπεί γ’ ὅσα γίγνεται ἡμῖν,
line_details.english: nor even the perfect eye of Zeus; since whatever befalls us,
line_details.note: Many editors understand an implicit οὐδὲ (“nor even”) before Διὸς ὄμμα to fit the sense; I translate accordingly.

line_details.greek: Μοῖρά τε καὶ Διὸς ο ἶδε νόος δι ὰπαντὸς ἅπαντα.
line_details.english: Moira and the mind of Zeus know all things through and through.
line_details.note: διὰ παντὸς ἅπαντα = “through and through all things,” i.e., completely, universally.

text.english: But come to me, airy ones, soft-minded, gentle of spirit, Atrope, and Lachesis, and Klotho, come, nobly-sired, nocturnal, unseen, unchangeable, ever unwearied, all-giving, removers of Ananke for mortals, Moirai, hear my holy libations and prayers, coming to the mystai, secretly easing pains with kindly counsel.
text.greek: ἀλλά μοι, ἀέριοι, μαλακόφρονες, ἠπιόθυμοι, Ἄτροπε, καὶ Λάχεσι, Κλωθώ, μόλετ’, εὐπατέρειαι, νυκτέριοι, ἀφανεῖς, ἀμετάτροποι, αἰὲν ἀτειρε ῖς, παντοδότειραι, ἀφαιρέτιδες θνητοῖσιν ἀνάγκης, Μοῖραι, ἀκούσατ’ ἐμῶν ὁσίων λοιβ ῶν τε καὶ εὐχῶν, ἐρχόμεναι μύσταις λαθιπήμονες εὔφρονι βουλ ῇ.

line_details.greek: ἀλλά μοι, ἀέριοι , μαλακόφρονες, ἠπιόθυμοι,
line_details.english: But come to me, airy ones, soft-minded, gentle of spirit,
line_details.note: ἀέριοι “airy” marks their subtle, aetherial nature; ἠπιόθυμοι “gentle-spirited.”

line_details.greek: Ἄτροπε, καὶ Λάχεσι, Κλωθώ, μόλετ’, εὐπατέρειαι,
line_details.english: Atrope, and Lachesis, and Klotho, come, nobly-sired,
line_details.note: εὐπατέρειαι = “nobly-sired”; though the Moirai are daughters of Nyx in some theogonies, the epithet stresses noble lineage rather than a specific father.

line_details.greek: νυκτέριοι, ἀφανεῖς, ἀμετάτροποι, αἰὲν ἀτειρε ῖς,
line_details.english: nocturnal, unseen, unchangeable, ever unwearied,
line_details.note: ἀμετάτροποι = “unchangeable, not to be turned”; ἀτειρεῖς = “unwearied/unyielding.”

line_details.greek: παντοδότειραι, ἀφαιρέτιδες θνητοῖσιν ἀνάγκης,
line_details.english: all-giving, removers of Ananke for mortals,
line_details.note: ἀφαιρέτιδες θνητοῖσιν ἀνάγκης can mean “removers of Ananke (Necessity) for mortals” or “those who take away (what is due) by Necessity”; I adopt the beneficent nuance suited to prayer.

line_details.greek: Μοῖραι, ἀκούσατ’ ἐμῶν ὁσίων λοιβ ῶν τε καὶ εὐχῶν,
line_details.english: Moirai, hear my holy libations and prayers,
line_details.note: ὁσίων modifies both libations and prayers, marking them as ritually proper/holy offerings.

line_details.greek: ἐρχόμεναι μύσταις λαθιπήμονες εὔφρονι βουλ ῇ.
line_details.english: coming to the mystai, secretly easing pains with kindly counsel.
